Kana: すまほをつかう
Usage note: 使う is the ordinary broad verb for operating or making use of a smartphone. The device is marked with を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 電車の中では音を消してスマホを使う。
Example 1 (English): I use my smartphone with the sound off on the train.
Example 2 (Japanese): 授業中はスマホを使わないでください。
Example 2 (English): Please do not use your smartphone during class.
Contrast: スマホで調べる: use a smartphone as the means of searching / スマホを見る: look at or check the phone
Misuse note: スマホで使う needs another object: このアプリをスマホで使う. When the phone itself is the object being used, say スマホを使う.

Kana: ほんをとじる
Usage note: 閉じる is the standard transitive verb for bringing the covers or pages of a book together.
Example 1 (Japanese): 読み終わったところで本を閉じた。
Example 1 (English): I closed the book when I reached the end.
Example 2 (Japanese): 先生の合図で、学生たちは本を閉じた。
Example 2 (English): At the teacher's signal, the students closed their books.
Contrast: 本を開く: open a book / 本をしまう: put a book away
Misuse note: 閉める is used for doors, windows, lids, and shops. Use 閉じる for a book, eyes, or an open computer file.

Kana: かいわをれんしゅうする
Usage note: The skill or activity being practiced is marked with を before 練習する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 毎朝、先生と日本語の会話を練習している。
Example 1 (English): Every morning, I practice Japanese conversation with my teacher.
Example 2 (Japanese): 旅行で使う短い会話を二人で練習した。
Example 2 (English): The two of us practiced short conversations for the trip.
Contrast: 会話の練習をする: do conversation practice / 話す練習をする: practice speaking
Misuse note: 会話に練習する is not the normal particle pattern. Use 会話を練習する or 会話の練習をする.

Kana: いいてんき
Usage note: いい naturally evaluates 天気 as pleasant or favorable. In careful writing, よい天気 is also possible.
Example 1 (Japanese): 今日はいい天気だから、公園まで歩こう。
Example 1 (English): The weather is nice today, so let's walk to the park.
Example 2 (Japanese): 週末もいい天気が続くらしい。
Example 2 (English): It looks as though the nice weather will continue through the weekend.
Contrast: 晴れた天気: sunny weather / 悪い天気: bad weather
Misuse note: 強い can describe wind, rain, or sunlight, but 強い天気 is not the ordinary way to say 'good weather.'

Kana: しごとにやくだつ
Usage note: The area or purpose that benefits is marked with に before 役立つ.
Example 1 (Japanese): この資格は海外との仕事に役立つ。
Example 1 (English): This qualification is useful for work with overseas clients.
Example 2 (Japanese): 留学中に学んだことが今の仕事に役立っている。
Example 2 (English): What I learned while studying abroad is useful in my current job.
Contrast: 仕事で使う: use something at work / 仕事に生かす: apply a skill or experience to work
Misuse note: Do not mark 仕事 with を. If a person actively puts something to use, use 経験を仕事に役立てる with transitive 役立てる.

Kana: おうぼをしめきる
Usage note: 締め切る marks the point after which submissions or applications are no longer accepted.
Example 1 (Japanese): 定員に達したため、予定より早く応募を締め切った。
Example 1 (English): Applications closed earlier than planned because all places were filled.
Example 2 (Japanese): コンテストの応募は金曜日で締め切ります。
Example 2 (English): Entries for the contest close on Friday.
Contrast: 応募を受け付ける: accept applications / 募集を終了する: end recruitment
Misuse note: 締め切る takes the applications or submissions as its object. 締め切り is the corresponding noun meaning deadline.

Kana: りょうりをつくる
Meaning: to cook; to make a dish
Usage note: 作る is the broad everyday verb for preparing a dish or meal. 料理する focuses more directly on the act of cooking.
Example 1 (Japanese): 冷蔵庫にある野菜で簡単な料理を作った。
Example 1 (English): I made a simple dish with the vegetables in the refrigerator.
Example 2 (Japanese): 休日は家族のために料理を作る。
Example 2 (English): On my days off, I cook for my family.
Contrast: 料理をする: cook as an activity / 食事を用意する: prepare a meal
Misuse note: 建てる is for erecting buildings. Use 作る for food, and use 料理する when the cooking activity itself is the focus.

Kana: ていきゅうびをかくにんする
Meaning: to check a business's regular closing day
Usage note: 確認する takes the information being checked as its direct object with を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 出かける前に店の定休日を確認した。
Example 1 (English): I checked the shop's regular closing day before going out.
Example 2 (Japanese): 公式サイトで美術館の定休日を確認してください。
Example 2 (English): Please check the museum's regular closing day on its official website.
Contrast: 営業時間を確認する: check business hours / 臨時休業を確認する: confirm a temporary closure
Misuse note: 定休日に確認する means 'check on the regular closing day.' To check which day it is, mark 定休日 with を.

Kana: へいかんじかんをかくにんする
Usage note: 閉館時間 is the time a facility such as a museum, library, or hall closes. It is checked with を確認する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 展示を見る前に閉館時間を確認しておこう。
Example 1 (English): Let's check the closing time before viewing the exhibition.
Example 2 (Japanese): 図書館の閉館時間を電話で確認した。
Example 2 (English): I checked the library's closing time by phone.
Contrast: 開館時間を確認する: check the opening time of a facility / 閉店時間を確認する: check a shop's closing time
Misuse note: Do not use 閉館時間 for every business. Choose 閉店時間 for a store and 終了時間 for an event.

Kana: りょこうにいく
Usage note: 旅行 is the purpose or activity of going and takes に. The destination itself can separately take へ or に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 来月、家族と北海道へ旅行に行く。
Example 1 (English): Next month, I'm going on a trip to Hokkaido with my family.
Example 2 (Japanese): 卒業前に友達と旅行に行きたい。
Example 2 (English): I want to take a trip with my friends before graduation.
Contrast: 旅行する: travel / 出張に行く: go on a business trip
Misuse note: 行く is intransitive, so 旅行 is not marked with を here. Use を with 旅行を計画する or 旅行を楽しむ.

Kana: のりつぎじかんがみじかい
Meaning: to have a short connection time
Usage note: The duration being evaluated is the subject of 短い and is marked with が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 乗り継ぎ時間が短いので、到着後すぐ次の搭乗口へ向かった。
Example 1 (English): The connection was short, so I went straight to the next gate after landing.
Example 2 (Japanese): この便は乗り継ぎ時間が短すぎて不安だ。
Example 2 (English): I'm worried that this flight leaves too little time for the connection.
Contrast: 待ち時間が長い: the waiting time is long / 乗り継ぎに間に合う: make the connection
Misuse note: An adjective predicate takes が here, not を. Use を only with a transitive verb such as 乗り継ぎ時間を短縮する.

Kana: よていをきょうゆうする
Meaning: to share a schedule or plans
Usage note: 共有する takes the information or resource being shared with を. The people sharing it can be marked with と.
Example 1 (Japanese): 家族の予定をカレンダーアプリで共有している。
Example 1 (English): We share the family's schedule in a calendar app.
Example 2 (Japanese): 会議の前に全員で今日の予定を共有した。
Example 2 (English): Before the meeting, everyone reviewed and shared today's schedule.
Contrast: 予定を知らせる: tell someone the plan / 情報を共有する: share information
Misuse note: The shared item takes を. Use Xと予定を共有する for 'share the schedule with X.'

Kana: どくしょをしてすごす
Usage note: Xをして過ごす names the activity used to fill a period of time. 読書する is also possible, but this pattern highlights how the time is spent.
Example 1 (Japanese): 雨の日は家で読書をして過ごすことが多い。
Example 1 (English): On rainy days, I often spend my time reading at home.
Example 2 (Japanese): 連休は図書館で読書をして過ごした。
Example 2 (English): I spent the holiday reading at the library.
Contrast: 本を読んで過ごす: spend the time reading books / のんびり過ごす: spend the time relaxing
Misuse note: Use する for the activity 読書. 作る does not combine with 読書 to mean 'do some reading.'

Kana: せいどをりようする
Meaning: to make use of a system or program
Usage note: 利用する is natural for making practical use of an available system, service, facility, or benefit.
Example 1 (Japanese): 育児休業の制度を利用して半年休んだ。
Example 1 (English): I used the parental-leave program and took six months off.
Example 2 (Japanese): 条件を満たせば、補助制度を利用できます。
Example 2 (English): You can use the subsidy program if you meet the conditions.
Contrast: 制度を活用する: make effective use of a system / 制度を導入する: introduce a system
Misuse note: Mark the system with を. If a person is exploited by a system, the roles and particles are different, as in 制度に利用される.

Japanese: 一朝一夕にはいかない
Kana: いっちょういっせきにはいかない
Usage note: This fixed expression says that a difficult result cannot be achieved in a single morning and evening. It normally appears with a negative predicate.
Example 1 (Japanese): 自然な発音を身につけるのは一朝一夕にはいかない。
Example 1 (English): Natural pronunciation cannot be mastered overnight.
Example 2 (Japanese): 信頼関係は一朝一夕には築けない。
Example 2 (English): A relationship of trust cannot be built overnight.
Contrast: すぐにはできない: cannot be done immediately / 時間がかかる: takes time
Misuse note: The idiom normally combines with には and a negative expression such as いかない, できない, or 身につかない.

Kana: ぺーじをひらく
Meaning: to open to a page; open a page
Usage note: 開く is read ひらく here and is used for opening a book to a page or opening a webpage.
Example 1 (Japanese): 教科書の四十二ページを開いてください。
Example 1 (English): Please open your textbook to page forty-two.
Example 2 (Japanese): リンクを押すと、新しいページが開く。
Example 2 (English): Pressing the link opens a new page.
Contrast: 本を開く: open a book / ページをめくる: turn a page
Misuse note: 起こす means raise, wake, or cause. Use 開く for opening a book or webpage, and distinguish transitive ページを開く from intransitive ページが開く.

Kana: ほんをよむ
Usage note: 読む is the standard verb for engaging with the written content of a book.
Example 1 (Japanese): 寝る前に三十分だけ本を読む。
Example 1 (English): I read a book for just thirty minutes before bed.
Example 2 (Japanese): 子どもに毎晩同じ本を読んでいる。
Example 2 (English): I read the same book to my child every night.
Contrast: 本を見る: look at or consult a book / 本を読み返す: reread a book
Misuse note: Use 聞く for audio and 読む for written text. In 子どもに本を読む, に marks the person being read to.

Kana: ふくをうる
Usage note: The item transferred in exchange for money is the direct object of 売る and takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 着なくなった服をフリーマーケットで売った。
Example 1 (English): I sold clothes I no longer wear at a flea market.
Example 2 (Japanese): この店では古着を安く売っている。
Example 2 (English): This shop sells used clothes cheaply.
Contrast: 服を買う: buy clothes / 服を譲る: give or transfer clothes to someone
Misuse note: 服に売る incorrectly makes the clothing sound like the recipient. Say 人に服を売る when naming the buyer.

Kana: まどをあける
Usage note: 開ける is the everyday transitive verb when a person opens a window, door, container, or gap.
Example 1 (Japanese): 空気を入れ替えるために窓を開けた。
Example 1 (English): I opened the window to let in fresh air.
Example 2 (Japanese): 寒いので、窓を少しだけ開けてください。
Example 2 (English): It's cold, so please open the window only a little.
Contrast: 窓が開く: the window opens / 窓を閉める: close the window
Misuse note: Do not mix the two verb patterns. A person opens it with 窓を開ける; the resulting event is 窓が開く.

Kana: どあをしめる
Usage note: 閉める is the standard transitive verb for a person closing a door, window, lid, or shop.
Example 1 (Japanese): 部屋を出るときにドアを静かに閉めた。
Example 1 (English): I closed the door quietly when I left the room.
Example 2 (Japanese): 冷房中なのでドアを閉めてください。
Example 2 (English): Please close the door while the air conditioning is on.
Contrast: ドアが閉まる: the door closes / ドアを開ける: open the door
Misuse note: Use を with the transitive verb 閉める. Use が with the intransitive verb 閉まる when no agent is expressed.

Kana: べっどでねる
Usage note: で marks the place where the action of sleeping occurs. に can mark getting into or lying down on the bed, but not the ordinary activity location in this meaning.
Example 1 (Japanese): 旅行中も自分のベッドで寝るのが恋しかった。
Example 1 (English): Even while traveling, I missed sleeping in my own bed.
Example 2 (Japanese): 昨夜はソファではなく、ちゃんとベッドで寝た。
Example 2 (English): Last night I slept properly in bed instead of on the sofa.
Contrast: ベッドに入る: get into bed / ベッドに横になる: lie down on the bed
Misuse note: 寝る is intransitive and does not take the bed as a を-object. Use で for the place of sleeping.

Kana: ざんぎょうがおおい
Meaning: to have a lot of overtime work
Usage note: The thing that exists in a large amount takes が before 多い. The person or workplace is usually the topic.
Example 1 (Japanese): 今月は決算前で残業が多い。
Example 1 (English): I have a lot of overtime this month because the fiscal closing is near.
Example 2 (Japanese): 残業が多い職場では働きたくない。
Example 2 (English): I do not want to work at a workplace with a lot of overtime.
Contrast: 残業をする: work overtime / 残業が続く: overtime continues
Misuse note: 多い is an adjective, so its subject takes が. Use を only with a verb, as in 残業を減らす.

Kana: ほんをかう
Usage note: The purchased item takes を; the place of purchase takes で, and the seller can take から.
Example 1 (Japanese): 駅前の書店で日本語の本を二冊買った。
Example 1 (English): I bought two Japanese books at the bookstore near the station.
Example 2 (Japanese): 電子版ではなく紙の本を買うことにした。
Example 2 (English): I decided to buy the print book rather than the digital edition.
Contrast: 本を借りる: borrow a book / 本を注文する: order a book
Misuse note: Use が only in a potential pattern such as 本が買える. In the ordinary active sentence, the purchased item takes を.

Kana: じかんをかんりする
Usage note: 管理する is used for controlling and organizing a resource such as time, money, inventory, or data.
Example 1 (Japanese): 複数の仕事を進めるには時間を上手に管理する必要がある。
Example 1 (English): To handle several tasks, you need to manage your time well.
Example 2 (Japanese): アプリで勉強時間を管理している。
Example 2 (English): I track and manage my study time with an app.
Contrast: 予定を立てる: make a schedule or plan / 時間を有効に使う: use time effectively
Misuse note: The managed resource takes を. A manager or system that performs the management is the subject, not marked with に.

Kana: さぎょうじかんをたんしゅくする
Usage note: The duration being reduced takes を. 作業時間 makes the type of time explicit and is common in efficiency discussions.
Example 1 (Japanese): 新しい機械で作業時間を三十分短縮できた。
Example 1 (English): The new machine reduced the working time by thirty minutes.
Example 2 (Japanese): 手順を見直して、作業時間を短縮した。
Example 2 (English): We reviewed the procedure and reduced the working time.
Contrast: 作業時間が短縮される: the working time is reduced / 時間を節約する: save time
Misuse note: Use を with active 短縮する. In the passive statement, say 作業時間が短縮される.

Kana: はやねはやおきのしゅうかん
Meaning: a habit of going to bed and getting up early
Usage note: 早寝早起き forms a fixed pair, and の links that routine to 習慣.
Example 1 (Japanese): 子どものころに早寝早起きの習慣が身についた。
Example 1 (English): I developed the habit of going to bed and getting up early as a child.
Example 2 (Japanese): 早寝早起きの習慣を続けるため、夜十一時には寝る。
Example 2 (English): To maintain my early-to-bed, early-to-rise routine, I go to bed by eleven.
Contrast: 生活習慣: lifestyle habit / 規則正しい生活: regular daily routine
Misuse note: Do not build the pair by inflecting 早い. 早寝 and 早起き are established noun forms.

Kana: じかんをたんしゅくする
Usage note: 短縮する takes the duration or time period being reduced as its を-object.
Example 1 (Japanese): オンライン受付に変えて待ち時間を短縮した。
Example 1 (English): Switching to online reception shortened the waiting time.
Example 2 (Japanese): 会議時間を十五分短縮することになった。
Example 2 (English): We decided to shorten the meeting by fifteen minutes.
Contrast: 時間が短縮される: the time is reduced / 時間を節約する: save time
Misuse note: Use を in an active sentence. With が, use the passive pattern 時間が短縮される.

Kana: はをみがく
Usage note: 磨く covers brushing teeth as well as polishing surfaces and refining skills.
Example 1 (Japanese): 朝食のあとで歯を磨いた。
Example 1 (English): I brushed my teeth after breakfast.
Example 2 (Japanese): 寝る前に必ず歯を磨いている。
Example 2 (English): I always brush my teeth before bed.
Contrast: 歯をみがく: same phrase in kana / 口をゆすぐ: rinse one's mouth
Misuse note: 洗う is used for washing with water, but the standard verb for brushing teeth is 磨く.

Kana: かおをあらう
Usage note: The body part being washed is the direct object of 洗う and takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 起きたら、まず冷たい水で顔を洗う。
Example 1 (English): When I wake up, the first thing I do is wash my face with cold water.
Example 2 (Japanese): 化粧を落としてから顔を洗った。
Example 2 (English): I washed my face after removing my makeup.
Contrast: 手を洗う: wash one's hands / 顔を拭く: wipe one's face
Misuse note: Use を for the body part. に can mark a location for applying something, as in 顔に水をかける.

Kana: ぱそこんをつかう
Usage note: 使う is the broad everyday verb for operating or using a computer.
Example 1 (Japanese): 仕事では毎日パソコンを使う。
Example 1 (English): I use a computer every day at work.
Example 2 (Japanese): 図書館のパソコンを使って資料を調べた。
Example 2 (English): I used a library computer to research the material.
Contrast: パソコンで作業する: work on a computer / パソコンを操作する: operate a computer
Misuse note: Use を when the computer is the thing used. Use で when it is the means: パソコンで書く.

Kana: こうざをかいせつする
Usage note: 開設する is the formal standard verb for establishing an account, office, website, or service.
Example 1 (Japanese): 給料を受け取るために銀行口座を開設した。
Example 1 (English): I opened a bank account to receive my salary.
Example 2 (Japanese): アプリから証券口座を開設できます。
Example 2 (English): You can open a securities account through the app.
Contrast: 口座を作る: create an account, conversational / 口座を解約する: close an account contract
Misuse note: 口座を閉じる is possible for closing an account, but opening one formally is 口座を開設する.

Kana: しゃわーをあびる
Usage note: 浴びる is the standard verb for receiving a shower over the body. シャワー takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 運動のあとでシャワーを浴びた。
Example 1 (English): I took a shower after exercising.
Example 2 (Japanese): 朝は短いシャワーを浴びるだけだ。
Example 2 (English): In the morning, I only take a quick shower.
Contrast: お風呂に入る: take a bath / 水を浴びる: be drenched or splash water over oneself
Misuse note: Use 浴びる for a shower. 入る combines with お風呂 or 温泉 because the person enters the bath.

Kana: ひまなじかん
Usage note: 暇 is a な-adjective before a noun, so it becomes 暇な時間.
Example 1 (Japanese): 暇な時間に旅行の写真を整理した。
Example 1 (English): I organized my travel photos in my free time.
Example 2 (Japanese): 昼休みに暇な時間があれば電話します。
Example 2 (English): I'll call during lunch if I have a free moment.
Contrast: 空いた時間: time that has become available / 自由時間: free time allotted for personal use
Misuse note: Use な, not の, between 暇 and a noun. 暇だ is the sentence-final form.

Kana: おふろにはいる
Usage note: The bath is treated as the place entered, so お風呂 takes に before 入る.
Example 1 (Japanese): 夕食の前にお風呂に入った。
Example 1 (English): I took a bath before dinner.
Example 2 (Japanese): 疲れた日は早めにお風呂に入る。
Example 2 (English): On tiring days, I take a bath early.
Contrast: シャワーを浴びる: take a shower / 湯船につかる: soak in the bathtub
Misuse note: Use に with 入る. お風呂を入れる means prepare or fill the bath, not bathe oneself.

Kana: ふくをきる
Meaning: to put on or wear clothes for the upper body
Usage note: 着る is used for garments worn over the upper body or whole body, including shirts, coats, and dresses.
Example 1 (Japanese): 外が寒いので、暖かい服を着た。
Example 1 (English): It was cold outside, so I put on warm clothes.
Example 2 (Japanese): 彼女は新しい服を着て出かけた。
Example 2 (English): She went out wearing her new clothes.
Contrast: 靴を履く: put on shoes / 帽子をかぶる: put on a hat
Misuse note: Use 履く for footwear and lower-body garments. 着る is the broad default for tops and one-piece clothing.

Kana: くつをはく
Meaning: to put on or wear shoes
Usage note: 履く is used for things worn from below, including shoes, socks, trousers, and skirts.
Example 1 (Japanese): 玄関で靴を履いて外に出た。
Example 1 (English): I put on my shoes at the entrance and went outside.
Example 2 (Japanese): 雨の日は滑りにくい靴を履く。
Example 2 (English): On rainy days, I wear shoes that do not slip easily.
Contrast: 服を着る: put on clothes / 靴を脱ぐ: take off shoes
Misuse note: Do not use 着る for shoes. The kanji 履く is also used for trousers and skirts.

Kana: でんきをつける
Usage note: In everyday speech, 電気 often means an electric light; つける means switch it on.
Example 1 (Japanese): 暗くなったので部屋の電気をつけた。
Example 1 (English): It grew dark, so I turned on the room light.
Example 2 (Japanese): 廊下の電気をつけたまま寝てしまった。
Example 2 (English): I fell asleep with the hall light on.
Contrast: 電気を消す: turn off the light / 明かりをつける: turn on a light
Misuse note: Use つける for switching on a light or appliance. 開ける is for opening doors, windows, and containers.

Kana: でんきをけす
Usage note: 消す is the standard transitive verb for switching off a light and for extinguishing flames.
Example 1 (Japanese): 最後に部屋を出る人が電気を消してください。
Example 1 (English): The last person to leave the room should turn off the light.
Example 2 (Japanese): 寝る前に台所の電気を消した。
Example 2 (English): I turned off the kitchen light before bed.
Contrast: 電気が消える: the light goes out / 電気をつける: turn on the light
Misuse note: Use transitive 消す when someone turns it off. Use intransitive 消える when the light goes out.

Kana: とけいをみる
Meaning: to look at the clock or one's watch
Usage note: 見る is used for visually checking a clock or watch. The intended device follows from context.
Example 1 (Japanese): 時計を見たら、もう十二時を過ぎていた。
Example 1 (English): When I looked at the clock, it was already past midnight.
Example 2 (Japanese): 何度も時計を見ながら友達を待った。
Example 2 (English): I waited for my friend, looking at my watch again and again.
Contrast: 時間を確認する: check the time, more explicit / 時計を確認する: check the clock or watch
Misuse note: 時計 is the device; 時間 is time itself. Use 時計を見る for the ordinary physical action.

Kana: てれびをみる
Usage note: 見る covers watching television and video content; テレビ can mean the device or television programming.
Example 1 (Japanese): 夕食のあとで家族とテレビを見る。
Example 1 (English): I watch television with my family after dinner.
Example 2 (Japanese): 最近はテレビを見ずに、配信でニュースを見ている。
Example 2 (English): Lately I watch the news online rather than on television.
Contrast: 番組を見る: watch a program / テレビをつける: turn on the television
Misuse note: 見る describes watching. つける only switches the device on and does not imply paying attention to it.

Kana: おんがくをきく
Usage note: 聴く emphasizes intentional, attentive listening. Everyday writing also commonly uses the more general kanji 聞く with music.
Example 1 (Japanese): 通勤中にイヤホンで音楽を聴いている。
Example 1 (English): I listen to music through earphones while commuting.
Example 2 (Japanese): 勉強するときは歌詞のない音楽を聴く。
Example 2 (English): When I study, I listen to music without lyrics.
Contrast: 音楽を聞く: common general-kanji spelling / 音が聞こえる: a sound can be heard
Misuse note: 聴く is not mandatory every time; 聞く is standard in everyday writing. Use 聞こえる for an involuntary audible sound.

Kana: よていがある
Usage note: The planned event or arrangement is presented as something that exists, so 予定 takes が before ある.
Example 1 (Japanese): 土曜日は家族と出かける予定がある。
Example 1 (English): I have plans to go out with my family on Saturday.
Example 2 (Japanese): 午後は会議の予定がある。
Example 2 (English): A meeting is scheduled for the afternoon.
Contrast: 予定を立てる: make plans / 用事がある: have something to do
Misuse note: Use が with ある. Use を only when a transitive verb acts on the plan, as in 予定を変更する.

Kana: よやくをする
Meaning: to make a reservation or appointment
Usage note: 予約をする is the broad neutral pattern for booking a service, seat, room, or appointment.
Example 1 (Japanese): 電話で歯医者の予約をした。
Example 1 (English): I made a dentist appointment by phone.
Example 2 (Japanese): 人気の店なので、一週間前に予約をした。
Example 2 (English): Because the restaurant is popular, I reserved a table a week ahead.
Contrast: 予約を取る: secure or make an appointment / 予約を取り消す: cancel a reservation
Misuse note: 作る is not the standard verb for a reservation. Use 予約する or 予約をする.

Kana: ひきだしをあける
Usage note: 開ける is the standard transitive verb for opening a drawer, door, window, or container.
Example 1 (Japanese): 机の引き出しを開けて、はさみを取り出した。
Example 1 (English): I opened the desk drawer and took out the scissors.
Example 2 (Japanese): 鍵がかかっていて引き出しを開けられない。
Example 2 (English): The drawer is locked, so I cannot open it.
Contrast: 引き出しが開く: the drawer opens / 引き出しを閉める: close a drawer
Misuse note: Use を with transitive 開ける. Potential 開けられる can change the subject marking in some contexts, so do not copy it into the basic pattern.

Kana: じゆうせきをりようする
Usage note: 利用する is natural for using an available service or seating category. 自由席 means seats not individually reserved.
Example 1 (Japanese): 混んでいない時間なら自由席を利用する。
Example 1 (English): When it is not crowded, I use non-reserved seating.
Example 2 (Japanese): 追加料金を避けるため、自由席を利用した。
Example 2 (English): I used non-reserved seating to avoid the additional charge.
Contrast: 指定席を予約する: reserve an assigned seat / 自由席に座る: sit in a non-reserved seat
Misuse note: The service used takes を. A particular seat occupied takes に with 座る.

Kana: じかんにせいげんがある
Usage note: The domain being restricted takes に, while 制限 is what exists and takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): この試験は時間に厳しい制限がある。
Example 1 (English): This examination has a strict time limit.
Example 2 (Japanese): 面会時間に制限があるか確認した。
Example 2 (English): I checked whether visiting hours were restricted.
Contrast: 時間制限がある: there is a time limit / 時間を制限する: restrict the time
Misuse note: Do not combine を with 制限がある. Use 時間を制限する only when 制限する is the active verb.

Kana: しげんをゆうこうにつかう
Usage note: 有効に is the adverbial form modifying 使う; the resource takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 限られた水資源を有効に使う方法を考えた。
Example 1 (English): We considered ways to use limited water resources effectively.
Example 2 (Japanese): 人材と予算を有効に使う必要がある。
Example 2 (English): We need to use our personnel and budget effectively.
Contrast: 資源を節約する: conserve resources / 資源を活用する: make practical use of resources
Misuse note: Use に to turn 有効 into an adverb before 使う. 有効で would require a following clause or different construction.

Kana: しゃしんをとる
Usage note: 撮る is the standard verb for taking photographs and recording video.
Example 1 (Japanese): 旅行先で家族の写真をたくさん撮った。
Example 1 (English): I took many photos of my family while traveling.
Example 2 (Japanese): ここでは写真を撮ってもいいですか。
Example 2 (English): May I take photos here?
Contrast: 動画を撮る: record a video / 写真に写る: appear in a photograph
Misuse note: 取る has the same pronunciation but means take or obtain more generally. Use the camera-related kanji 撮る for photos and video.

Kana: ほんをほんやくする
Usage note: The source text takes を; the source language takes から and the target language takes に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 彼女はその本を日本語から英語に翻訳した。
Example 1 (English): She translated the book from Japanese into English.
Example 2 (Japanese): 専門用語の多い本を翻訳するのは難しい。
Example 2 (English): Translating a book full of technical terms is difficult.
Contrast: 会議で通訳する: interpret at a meeting / 文章を訳す: translate a passage
Misuse note: Do not use 通訳する for a written book. 通訳 handles spoken communication; 翻訳 handles written text and subtitles.

Kana: ようじがある
Meaning: to have something to do; have an errand
Usage note: 用事 is a task, errand, or matter requiring attention; it is presented as existing with がある.
Example 1 (Japanese): 今日は銀行に用事がある。
Example 1 (English): I have some business at the bank today.
Example 2 (Japanese): 午後は用事があるので、先に帰ります。
Example 2 (English): I have something to take care of this afternoon, so I'll leave early.
Contrast: 予定がある: have plans or something scheduled / 用を済ませる: finish an errand
Misuse note: Use が with ある. 用事 can be deliberately vague, so state the task if the listener needs specifics.

Kana: いえにかえる
Usage note: 家に帰る is the ordinary way to say that someone returns home; the destination takes に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 仕事が終わったら、まっすぐ家に帰る。
Example 1 (English): I go straight home after work.
Example 2 (Japanese): 雨が降る前に家に帰ろう。
Example 2 (English): Let's go home before it rains.
Contrast: 家へ帰る: go home, with directional emphasis / 実家に帰る: return to one's family home
Misuse note: Use に or へ for the destination. を can mark a route or point of departure, not the destination of 帰る.

Kana: へやをそうじする
Usage note: The place being cleaned takes を with 掃除する. The shorter 部屋を掃除する is suitable as a reusable pattern.
Example 1 (Japanese): 土曜日の朝に自分の部屋を掃除する。
Example 1 (English): I clean my room on Saturday mornings.
Example 2 (Japanese): 来客の前に客間を掃除した。
Example 2 (English): I cleaned the guest room before our visitors arrived.
Contrast: 部屋を片付ける: tidy a room / 部屋に掃除機をかける: vacuum a room
Misuse note: Use を for the target of cleaning. 掃除する concerns dirt; 片付ける concerns disorder and objects left out.

Kana: だいどころでりょうりする
Usage note: で marks the place where the activity 料理する happens. 台所 is the everyday word for a home kitchen.
Example 1 (Japanese): 休日は家族と台所で料理する。
Example 1 (English): On days off, I cook with my family in the kitchen.
Example 2 (Japanese): 狭い台所で二人一緒に料理した。
Example 2 (English): The two of us cooked together in the small kitchen.
Contrast: 台所に立つ: work in the kitchen / 家で料理する: cook at home
Misuse note: Use で for an activity performed in a place. に is possible with verbs of existence or arrival, such as 台所にいる.

Kana: へやのおく
Meaning: the back or far end of a room
Usage note: 奥 refers to the area farthest from the entrance or viewpoint. の links the space to its far end.
Example 1 (Japanese): 季節外れの荷物は部屋の奥に置いてある。
Example 1 (English): The out-of-season belongings are kept at the back of the room.
Example 2 (Japanese): 部屋の奥から古い箱を取り出した。
Example 2 (English): I took an old box out from the back of the room.
Contrast: 部屋の中: inside the room / 廊下の突き当たり: the end of the corridor
Misuse note: Use の between the reference space and 奥. Choose 中 when depth or distance from the entrance is irrelevant.

Kana: てりょうりをつくる
Meaning: to make a home-cooked meal for someone
Usage note: 手料理 usually highlights food personally cooked for other people, often with warmth or care.
Example 1 (Japanese): 誕生日に家族のために手料理を作った。
Example 1 (English): I made a home-cooked meal for my family on their birthday.
Example 2 (Japanese): 今度、得意な手料理を作ってあげたい。
Example 2 (English): Next time, I'd like to cook my specialty for them.
Contrast: 料理を作る: cook or make food / 手料理を振る舞う: serve one's home cooking
Misuse note: 作る is natural for preparing the food. 振る舞う shifts the focus to serving it to guests.

Kana: りょうりにこる
Meaning: to become deeply interested in cooking
Usage note: Xに凝る means to devote unusual enthusiasm, time, or attention to X as a hobby or pursuit.
Example 1 (Japanese): 在宅勤務を始めてから料理に凝っている。
Example 1 (English): I've become deeply interested in cooking since I started working from home.
Example 2 (Japanese): 父は最近、燻製料理に凝っている。
Example 2 (English): My father has recently gotten really into smoked food.
Contrast: 料理に夢中になる: become absorbed in cooking / 料理にこだわる: be particular about cooking
Misuse note: The interest takes に. 凝った料理 is a different pattern meaning elaborate or ingeniously prepared food.

Kana: おふくろのあじ
Meaning: the taste of one's mother's home cooking
Usage note: This set phrase evokes familiar food cooked by one's mother. It often appears in nostalgic, traditionally male speech.
Example 1 (Japanese): この煮物を食べると、お袋の味を思い出す。
Example 1 (English): This simmered dish reminds me of my mother's cooking.
Example 2 (Japanese): 店の看板には『お袋の味』と書かれていた。
Example 2 (English): The restaurant sign advertised 'mother's home cooking.'
Contrast: 母の味: mother's cooking, more neutral / 家庭の味: the taste of home cooking
Misuse note: お袋 is informal and may sound old-fashioned or overly familiar. Use 母の味 or 家庭の味 when that voice is unsuitable.

Kana: へやをかたづける
Usage note: 片付ける means putting scattered objects away and restoring order; the space being tidied takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 友達が来る前に部屋を片付けた。
Example 1 (English): I tidied my room before my friend came over.
Example 2 (Japanese): 使った物を戻せば、部屋を片付けやすい。
Example 2 (English): A room is easier to tidy if you return things after using them.
Contrast: 部屋を掃除する: clean a room / 物を片付ける: put things away
Misuse note: Use transitive 片付ける with を. 部屋が片付く uses the intransitive form and describes the room becoming tidy.

Kana: せいけつにたもつ
Meaning: to keep something clean and hygienic
Usage note: The に-form marks the maintained state, while 保つ expresses keeping that state over time.
Example 1 (Japanese): 調理器具はいつも清潔に保ってください。
Example 1 (English): Please keep the cooking utensils clean at all times.
Example 2 (Japanese): 浴室を清潔に保つには換気も必要だ。
Example 2 (English): Ventilation is also needed to keep a bathroom clean.
Contrast: きれいに保つ: keep clean or attractive / 衛生を保つ: maintain hygiene
Misuse note: Use 清潔に before 保つ. 清潔で is used to connect clauses, as in 清潔で使いやすい.

Kana: かていりょうりをならう
Meaning: to learn home-style cooking from someone
Usage note: 習う presents a skill or subject learned through instruction; the subject takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 地域の教室で日本の家庭料理を習っている。
Example 1 (English): I'm learning Japanese home-style cooking at a local class.
Example 2 (Japanese): 祖母から郷土の家庭料理を習った。
Example 2 (English): I learned local home cooking from my grandmother.
Contrast: 家庭料理を学ぶ: study home cooking / 料理教室に通う: attend a cooking class
Misuse note: Use を for what is learned and から or に for the teacher. 通う instead selects the school or class as a destination.

Kana: ふろにはいる
Usage note: 風呂に入る is the standard expression for bathing; に marks what one enters.
Example 1 (Japanese): 寝る前にゆっくり風呂に入る。
Example 1 (English): I take a relaxing bath before bed.
Example 2 (Japanese): 今日は銭湯で風呂に入った。
Example 2 (English): I had a bath at a public bathhouse today.
Contrast: 風呂に入れる: put someone in the bath / シャワーを浴びる: take a shower
Misuse note: Use に with intransitive 入る. 風呂を入れる usually means preparing the bath, depending on context.

Kana: ごみをだす
Meaning: to put out the rubbish for collection
Usage note: In household contexts, ゴミを出す commonly means taking rubbish to the designated collection point.
Example 1 (Japanese): 火曜日の朝に燃えるゴミを出す。
Example 1 (English): I put out the burnable rubbish on Tuesday morning.
Example 2 (Japanese): 収集日の前夜にはゴミを出さないでください。
Example 2 (English): Please do not put out rubbish the night before collection day.
Contrast: ゴミを捨てる: throw rubbish away / ゴミが出る: rubbish is produced
Misuse note: Use を with the deliberate action 出す. Local sorting and collection rules determine when and where the phrase applies.

Kana: せんたくきをまわす
Usage note: 回す is a common conversational verb for operating a washing machine through a wash cycle.
Example 1 (Japanese): 朝食の前に洗濯機を回した。
Example 1 (English): I ran the washing machine before breakfast.
Example 2 (Japanese): 洗濯機を回している間に床を掃除する。
Example 2 (English): I clean the floor while the washing machine is running.
Contrast: 洗濯機を動かす: operate or move the washer / 洗濯をする: do the laundry
Misuse note: 回す is everyday wording. In manuals or formal instructions, 運転する may be used for machine operation.

Kana: せんたくものをほす
Meaning: to hang laundry out to dry
Usage note: 干す means exposing wet items to air or sun so they dry; the laundry takes を and the location often takes に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 晴れているので、ベランダに洗濯物を干した。
Example 1 (English): Because it is sunny, I hung the laundry on the balcony.
Example 2 (Japanese): 雨の日は浴室に洗濯物を干す。
Example 2 (English): On rainy days, I hang the laundry in the bathroom to dry.
Contrast: 洗濯物が乾く: the laundry dries / 洗濯物を部屋干しする: dry laundry indoors
Misuse note: Use transitive 干す for the person's action and intransitive 乾く for the resulting drying.

Kana: せんたくものをとりこむ
Meaning: to bring in dry or drying laundry
Usage note: For household laundry, 取り込む means removing it from the line or rack and bringing it indoors.
Example 1 (Japanese): 雨が降りそうなので、洗濯物を取り込んだ。
Example 1 (English): It looked like rain, so I brought the laundry in.
Example 2 (Japanese): 暗くなる前に洗濯物を取り込んでね。
Example 2 (English): Bring in the laundry before it gets dark, okay?
Contrast: 洗濯物を干す: hang laundry to dry / 洗濯物を畳む: fold the laundry
Misuse note: Use 取り込む for bringing laundry inside. 取り入れる is possible in other contexts but is not the ordinary household pairing here.

Kana: ちんたいけいやくをむすぶ
Meaning: to sign or enter into a rental agreement
Usage note: 契約を結ぶ is the conventional formal pairing for entering an agreement; 賃貸 specifies a rental.
Example 1 (Japanese): 入居前に不動産会社と賃貸契約を結んだ。
Example 1 (English): I entered into a rental agreement with the estate agent before moving in.
Example 2 (Japanese): 賃貸契約を結ぶ前に、解約条件を確認した。
Example 2 (English): I checked the cancellation terms before entering the rental agreement.
Contrast: 契約書に署名する: sign the contract document / 賃貸契約を更新する: renew a rental agreement
Misuse note: 署名する describes signing the document; 結ぶ describes establishing the contractual relationship.

Kana: せんたくものをたたむ
Usage note: 畳む means folding flexible items into a smaller, orderly form; laundry is a frequent object.
Example 1 (Japanese): 乾いた洗濯物を畳んで、棚にしまった。
Example 1 (English): I folded the dry laundry and put it on the shelf.
Example 2 (Japanese): テレビを見ながら洗濯物を畳んだ。
Example 2 (English): I folded the laundry while watching television.
Contrast: 服を畳む: fold clothes / 洗濯物をしまう: put the laundry away
Misuse note: 折る often means bending or breaking along a line. Use 畳む for neatly folding clothes, bedding, and similar items.

Kana: そうじきをかける
Usage note: 掃除機をかける is the established everyday pairing for vacuuming. The area may take に or be understood from context.
Example 1 (Japanese): 週末に居間と廊下に掃除機をかける。
Example 1 (English): I vacuum the living room and hallway on weekends.
Example 2 (Japanese): 音が響くので、夜は掃除機をかけない。
Example 2 (English): I don't vacuum at night because the noise carries.
Contrast: 床を掃く: sweep the floor / 部屋を掃除する: clean the room
Misuse note: Use 掃除機をかける for the action. 掃除機を使う is grammatical but less specific about vacuuming.

Kana: つくえをまどぎわにうつす
Meaning: to move a desk beside the window
Usage note: The object moved takes を, and its new location takes に with transitive 移す.
Example 1 (Japanese): 明るい場所で作業するため、机を窓際に移した。
Example 1 (English): I moved the desk beside the window so I could work in a bright spot.
Example 2 (Japanese): 模様替えで机を窓際に移そうと思う。
Example 2 (English): I'm thinking of moving the desk beside the window when I rearrange the room.
Contrast: 机が窓際に移る: the desk moves to the window / 机を動かす: move the desk
Misuse note: Use 移す when someone moves the object. 移る is intransitive and makes the moved item the subject.

Kana: きゃくをへやにとおす
Meaning: to show a guest into a room
Usage note: 人を場所に通す is a hospitality pattern meaning to admit or show someone into that place.
Example 1 (Japanese): 玄関で挨拶してから、客を応接室に通した。
Example 1 (English): After greeting the guest at the entrance, I showed them into the reception room.
Example 2 (Japanese): 到着した客を先に部屋に通してください。
Example 2 (English): Please show the guest who has arrived into the room first.
Contrast: 客を招き入れる: invite a guest inside / 客が部屋に入る: the guest enters the room
Misuse note: Mark the guest with を and the destination with に. 通る is the related intransitive verb.

Kana: まどからうみをながめる
Meaning: to gaze at the sea from a window
Usage note: から marks the viewpoint, while the scene observed takes を with 眺める.
Example 1 (Japanese): 朝は窓から海を眺めながらコーヒーを飲む。
Example 1 (English): In the morning, I drink coffee while gazing at the sea through the window.
Example 2 (Japanese): ホテルの窓から夜景を眺めた。
Example 2 (English): I admired the night view from the hotel window.
Contrast: 窓から海が見える: the sea is visible from the window / 海を見る: look at the sea
Misuse note: Use 見える for spontaneous visibility. Use 眺める when someone intentionally takes in the view.

Kana: かぐをすえる
Meaning: to install or set furniture firmly in place
Usage note: 据える means placing something substantial in a chosen position, often with an expectation that it will remain there.
Example 1 (Japanese): 壁際に大きな収納家具を据えた。
Example 1 (English): We installed a large storage unit against the wall.
Example 2 (Japanese): 部屋の中央に低いテーブルを据えた。
Example 2 (English): We set a low table in the center of the room.
Contrast: 家具を置く: put or place furniture / 机を据え付ける: install a desk or fixture
Misuse note: Use を with transitive 据える. For ordinary, easily moved items, 置く is usually the more natural choice.

Kana: へやのすんぽうをはかる
Usage note: 寸法 refers to measured dimensions such as length, width, and height; the measured dimensions take を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 家具を買う前に部屋の寸法を測った。
Example 1 (English): I measured the room before buying furniture.
Example 2 (Japanese): メジャーを使って窓枠の寸法を測る。
Example 2 (English): I use a tape measure to measure the window frame.
Contrast: 部屋の広さを測る: measure the room's size / 長さを測る: measure the length
Misuse note: Use 測る for length, area, and other quantities. 図る and 計る share the reading but have different standard uses.

Kana: まどからそとをのぞく
Meaning: to peer outside through a window
Usage note: のぞく describes looking into or through a limited opening, often briefly or cautiously; から marks the viewpoint.
Example 1 (Japanese): 物音がしたので、窓から外をのぞいた。
Example 1 (English): I heard a noise, so I peered outside through the window.
Example 2 (Japanese): 子どもがカーテンの隙間から外をのぞいている。
Example 2 (English): The child is peeking outside through a gap in the curtains.
Contrast: 窓から外を見る: look outside through the window / 部屋をのぞく: peek into a room
Misuse note: Use のぞく when the restricted view or peeking manner matters. Use 見る for an unmarked act of looking.

Kana: しょっきをかたづける
Usage note: With 食器, 片付ける means clearing dishes from the table and returning or taking them to the proper place.
Example 1 (Japanese): 食事が終わったら、使った食器を片付ける。
Example 1 (English): After the meal, I clear away the dishes we used.
Example 2 (Japanese): 来客が食器を片付けるのを手伝ってくれた。
Example 2 (English): Our guests helped clear away the dishes.
Contrast: 食器を洗う: wash the dishes / テーブルを片付ける: clear the table
Misuse note: Use transitive 片付ける with を. 食器が片付く describes the dishes being cleared or the task getting done.

Kana: いえをるすにする
Usage note: 家を留守にする means no resident is at home for a period; 留守 is the resulting state.
Example 1 (Japanese): 旅行で三日ほど家を留守にする。
Example 1 (English): I'll be away from home for about three days on a trip.
Example 2 (Japanese): 長く家を留守にするときは新聞を止める。
Example 2 (English): I suspend newspaper delivery when I will be away for a long time.
Contrast: 家を空ける: be away from home / 留守番をする: stay behind and mind the house
Misuse note: Use 家を with 留守にする. A person who remains to watch the home does 留守番, not 留守.

Kana: しゅうのうによゆうがある
Usage note: Xに余裕がある says there is room, time, or capacity to spare in X; here X is household storage.
Example 1 (Japanese): この部屋は収納に余裕がある。
Example 1 (English): This room has plenty of spare storage capacity.
Example 2 (Japanese): 棚を整理したら収納に少し余裕ができた。
Example 2 (English): After organizing the shelves, I gained a little spare storage space.
Contrast: 収納が多い: have ample storage / 収納に余裕がない: have no spare storage capacity
Misuse note: The domain takes に and 余裕 takes が. Use 収納スペースがある when you only mean that storage exists.

Kana: かじをぶんたんする
Usage note: 分担する means dividing a body of work among multiple people so each person takes a share.
Example 1 (Japanese): 同居を始める前に家事を分担する方法を話し合った。
Example 1 (English): Before living together, we discussed how to share the household chores.
Example 2 (Japanese): 私たちは料理と掃除の家事を分担している。
Example 2 (English): We divide the cooking and cleaning between us.
Contrast: 家事を手伝う: help with chores / 役割を分担する: divide responsibilities
Misuse note: Use を for the work divided. If only one person is treated as responsible, 手伝う may unintentionally reinforce that assumption.

Kana: じっかをはなれる
Usage note: 実家 is the family home one comes from, often where one's parents live; 離れる marks departure or separation.
Example 1 (Japanese): 就職を機に実家を離れた。
Example 1 (English): I left my family home when I started working.
Example 2 (Japanese): 大学進学まで実家を離れたことがなかった。
Example 2 (English): I had never lived away from my family home before university.
Contrast: 実家を出る: move out of one's family home / 故郷を離れる: leave one's hometown
Misuse note: The place left takes を. Use 故郷 for a broader hometown or home region rather than the household itself.

Kana: いえがこいしい
Usage note: Xが恋しい expresses an aching wish to see or return to someone, somewhere, or something absent.
Example 1 (Japanese): 留学して一か月たつと、家が恋しくなった。
Example 1 (English): After a month abroad, I began to miss home.
Example 2 (Japanese): 家が恋しいときは家族に電話する。
Example 2 (English): When I miss home, I call my family.
Contrast: 故郷が恋しい: miss one's hometown / 家に帰りたい: want to go home
Misuse note: The object of longing normally takes が. 懐かしい instead describes something as fondly familiar when recalled or encountered.

Kana: ふろをわかす
Usage note: 風呂を沸かす conventionally means heating or preparing bathwater, including operating an automatic bath system.
Example 1 (Japanese): 冷える夜は早めに風呂を沸かす。
Example 1 (English): On cold nights, I prepare the bath early.
Example 2 (Japanese): 帰宅時間に合わせて風呂を沸かしておいた。
Example 2 (English): I had the bath ready for the time they came home.
Contrast: お湯を沸かす: boil or heat water / 風呂が沸く: the bath becomes ready
Misuse note: Use transitive 沸かす when someone prepares it and intransitive 沸く when it becomes hot or ready.

Kana: といれをそうじする
Meaning: to clean the toilet or bathroom
Usage note: In Japan, トイレ can refer to the toilet room as well as the fixture; the intended scope follows from context.
Example 1 (Japanese): 週に二回トイレを掃除する。
Example 1 (English): I clean the toilet twice a week.
Example 2 (Japanese): 来客の前にトイレを掃除しておいた。
Example 2 (English): I cleaned the toilet before our guests arrived.
Contrast: 便器を掃除する: clean the toilet bowl / 浴室を掃除する: clean the bathroom
Misuse note: The target takes を. Use 浴室 for the separate bathing area rather than translating every English 'bathroom' as トイレ.

Kana: たくはいびんをうけとる
Usage note: 宅配便 is a door-to-door parcel service; 受け取る focuses on the recipient taking delivery.
Example 1 (Japanese): 午前中に宅配便を受け取る予定だ。
Example 1 (English): I'm due to receive a courier delivery this morning.
Example 2 (Japanese): 不在だったので、夜に宅配便を受け取った。
Example 2 (English): I was out, so I received the delivery in the evening.
Contrast: 宅配便で送る: send by courier / 荷物を受け取る: receive a parcel
Misuse note: 受け取る is the standard neutral verb. もらう highlights receiving a favor or gift and is not always appropriate for delivery.

Kana: さらをあらう
Usage note: 皿を洗う is the basic household pairing; 皿 can stand for plates specifically or dishes collectively in context.
Example 1 (Japanese): 夕食のあとで皿を洗った。
Example 1 (English): I washed the dishes after dinner.
Example 2 (Japanese): 料理を作った人の代わりに私が皿を洗う。
Example 2 (English): I wash the dishes instead of the person who cooked.
Contrast: 食器を洗う: wash the tableware / 皿をすすぐ: rinse the plates
Misuse note: Use を with transitive 洗う. 食器 is the broader word when cups, bowls, and cutlery are included explicitly.

Kana: かいだんをのぼる
Usage note: With movement verbs, を can mark the route traversed; the stairs are the path, not a direct object in the English sense.
Example 1 (Japanese): エレベーターを使わず、階段を上った。
Example 1 (English): I went up the stairs instead of using the elevator.
Example 2 (Japanese): 重い荷物を持って階段を上るのは大変だ。
Example 2 (English): It is hard to climb the stairs carrying heavy luggage.
Contrast: 階段を下りる: go down the stairs / 二階に上がる: go upstairs
Misuse note: 階段を上る is the standard route pattern. に can mark a destination with 上がる, as in 二階に上がる.

Kana: やちんをはらう
Usage note: The charge being paid takes を with 払う; the recipient can take に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 毎月末に家賃を払う。
Example 1 (English): I pay the rent at the end of every month.
Example 2 (Japanese): 今月の家賃を大家さんに払った。
Example 2 (English): I paid this month's rent to the landlord.
Contrast: 家賃を振り込む: transfer the rent / 料金を払う: pay a fee
Misuse note: Use を for the payment and に for the recipient. 支払う is a slightly more formal alternative to 払う.

Kana: そうじをてっていする
Usage note: Xを徹底する means carrying X out fully and consistently, without leaving gaps.
Example 1 (Japanese): 食中毒を防ぐため、台所の掃除を徹底する。
Example 1 (English): We clean the kitchen thoroughly to prevent food poisoning.
Example 2 (Japanese): 引っ越し前に各部屋の掃除を徹底した。
Example 2 (English): We cleaned every room thoroughly before moving.
Contrast: 念入りに掃除する: clean carefully / 衛生管理を徹底する: enforce hygiene management
Misuse note: Use を when 徹底する is transitive. 徹底して掃除する reverses the structure but expresses a similar idea.

Kana: きたくがおそくなる
Usage note: 帰宅 is the event of returning home; が遅くなる says its time becomes later than usual or expected.
Example 1 (Japanese): 残業の日は帰宅が遅くなる。
Example 1 (English): I get home late on days when I work overtime.
Example 2 (Japanese): 電車が遅れて帰宅が遅くなった。
Example 2 (English): The train was delayed, so I got home late.
Contrast: 帰りが遅くなる: be late getting back / 遅く帰宅する: return home late
Misuse note: Use が with the event whose time changes. 帰宅を遅らせる instead means deliberately postponing the return.

Japanese: 料理にみりんを加える
Kana: りょうりにみりんをくわえる
Meaning: to add mirin to a dish
Usage note: The dish receiving an ingredient takes に, and the ingredient added takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 照りを出すため、料理にみりんを加えた。
Example 1 (English): I added mirin to the dish to give it a glaze.
Example 2 (Japanese): 煮汁にみりんを少し加えてください。
Example 2 (English): Please add a little mirin to the simmering liquid.
Contrast: 料理酒を加える: add cooking sake / みりんで味を調える: season with mirin
Misuse note: Keep the roles clear: destination に, added item を. 加える is neutral and works in recipes and explanations.

Kana: ごはんをたく
Usage note: 炊く is the standard verb for cooking rice or grain with water; ご飯 can mean cooked rice or a meal.
Example 1 (Japanese): 夕食に合わせてご飯を炊いた。
Example 1 (English): I cooked rice in time for dinner.
Example 2 (Japanese): 朝の分まで多めにご飯を炊く。
Example 2 (English): I cook extra rice for breakfast as well.
Contrast: 米を炊く: cook rice grain / お湯を沸かす: boil water
Misuse note: Use 炊く for rice. 焼く means grill or bake and produces a different dish.

Kana: ふとんをしく
Usage note: 敷く means spreading a flat item over a surface; bedding laid out for sleep takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 寝る前に和室へ布団を敷いた。
Example 1 (English): I laid out the futon in the Japanese-style room before bed.
Example 2 (Japanese): 来客用に二組の布団を敷いておく。
Example 2 (English): I'll lay out two futons for our guests.
Contrast: 布団を畳む: fold up a futon / ベッドを整える: make a bed
Misuse note: 置く only says where the item is placed. 敷く describes spreading it out ready for use.

Kana: ふとんをほす
Meaning: to air a futon in the sun
Usage note: 布団を干す means exposing bedding to sun and air to reduce moisture; the item takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 天気がいいのでベランダに布団を干した。
Example 1 (English): The weather was good, so I aired the futon on the balcony.
Example 2 (Japanese): 湿気が多い時期は、晴れた日に布団を干す。
Example 2 (English): In the humid season, I air the futon on sunny days.
Contrast: 洗濯物を干す: hang laundry to dry / 布団を乾燥させる: dry a futon
Misuse note: Use transitive 干す for the person's action. Do not confuse it with intransitive 乾く, 'to become dry.'

Kana: てをあらう
Usage note: The body part washed takes を; the cleaning agent can take で.
Example 1 (Japanese): 帰宅したら石けんで手を洗う。
Example 1 (English): I wash my hands with soap when I get home.
Example 2 (Japanese): 料理を始める前によく手を洗ってください。
Example 2 (English): Please wash your hands thoroughly before cooking.
Contrast: 手をすすぐ: rinse one's hands / 手洗いをする: wash one's hands
Misuse note: Use を with transitive 洗う. 手洗い can also refer to a washbasin or washing by hand, depending on context.

Kana: かぎをかける
Meaning: to lock a door or other closure
Usage note: 鍵をかける is the everyday pairing for securing a door, window, bicycle, or similar object with a lock.
Example 1 (Japanese): 外出するときは玄関の鍵をかける。
Example 1 (English): I lock the front door when I go out.
Example 2 (Japanese): 寝る前に窓の鍵をかけたか確認した。
Example 2 (English): I checked whether I had locked the window before bed.
Contrast: ドアを閉める: close the door / 鍵がかかっている: be locked
Misuse note: Closing and locking are separate actions: 閉める closes, while 鍵をかける locks.

Kana: かーてんをあける
Usage note: 開ける is used for moving curtains apart so the window or view is exposed.
Example 1 (Japanese): 朝起きたらカーテンを開ける。
Example 1 (English): I open the curtains when I get up in the morning.
Example 2 (Japanese): 日差しを入れるためにカーテンを開けた。
Example 2 (English): I opened the curtains to let in the sunlight.
Contrast: 窓を開ける: open the window / カーテンを閉める: close the curtains
Misuse note: Use 開ける for opening and つける for installing or attaching curtains.

Kana: かーてんをしめる
Usage note: 閉める is the standard transitive verb for closing curtains, doors, and windows.
Example 1 (Japanese): 暗くなったのでカーテンを閉めた。
Example 1 (English): It became dark, so I closed the curtains.
Example 2 (Japanese): 冷気を防ぐため、厚いカーテンを閉める。
Example 2 (English): I close the thick curtains to keep out the cold air.
Contrast: カーテンが閉まる: the curtains close / 雨戸を閉める: close the storm shutters
Misuse note: Use 閉める for the action and 閉まる for the intransitive change of state.

Japanese: 部屋が散らかっている
Kana: へやがちらかっている
Meaning: for a room to be messy
Usage note: 散らかっている describes the resulting state of things being out of place; the messy space takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 忙しくて部屋が散らかっている。
Example 1 (English): I've been busy, and my room is messy.
Example 2 (Japanese): 子どもが遊んだあとは居間が散らかっている。
Example 2 (English): The living room is messy after the children play.
Contrast: 部屋を散らかす: make a room messy / 部屋が汚れている: the room is dirty
Misuse note: Use が with intransitive 散らかる. Use を with transitive 散らかす when naming who caused the mess.

Kana: ゆかをふく
Meaning: to wipe or mop the floor
Usage note: 拭く removes moisture, dust, or dirt by rubbing with a cloth, sheet, or mop; the surface takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 飲み物をこぼしたので床を拭いた。
Example 1 (English): I spilled a drink, so I wiped the floor.
Example 2 (Japanese): 週末は台所の床を水拭きする。
Example 2 (English): On weekends, I damp-mop the kitchen floor.
Contrast: 床を掃く: sweep the floor / 雑巾で床を拭く: wipe the floor with a cleaning cloth
Misuse note: Use 拭く for wiping. 洗う is possible for washable outdoor floors but is not the default indoor-housework verb.

Kana: れいぞうこにしまう
Meaning: to put something away in the refrigerator
Usage note: しまう means returning or putting something into its proper storage place; that destination takes に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 残った料理は容器に入れて冷蔵庫にしまう。
Example 1 (English): I put leftovers in a container and store them in the refrigerator.
Example 2 (Japanese): 牛乳を使ったら、すぐ冷蔵庫にしまってね。
Example 2 (English): Put the milk back in the refrigerator right after you use it.
Contrast: 冷蔵庫に入れる: put in the refrigerator / 棚にしまう: put away on a shelf
Misuse note: The stored item takes を when stated, and the storage destination takes に. 冷蔵庫をしまう would mean putting the appliance away.

Kana: しょくたくをかこむ
Meaning: to gather around the dining table for a meal
Usage note: 食卓を囲む is an established image of people sitting together around a table and sharing a meal.
Example 1 (Japanese): 週末は家族全員で食卓を囲む。
Example 1 (English): On weekends, the whole family gathers around the table for a meal.
Example 2 (Japanese): 久しぶりに三世代で食卓を囲んだ。
Example 2 (English): For the first time in a while, three generations ate together around the table.
Contrast: 食卓に着く: sit down at the table / 一緒に食事をする: eat together
Misuse note: Use を with 囲む. 食卓に着く focuses on taking a seat, while 食卓を囲む highlights the group meal.

Kana: てごろなねだん
Usage note: 手ごろな describes something suited to one's needs or budget; with 値段 it usually means affordable without implying poor quality.
Example 1 (Japanese): この定食は量が多くて手ごろな値段だ。
Example 1 (English): This set meal is generous and reasonably priced.
Example 2 (Japanese): 手ごろな値段の炊飯器を探している。
Example 2 (English): I'm looking for a rice cooker at a reasonable price.
Contrast: 手ごろな価格: an affordable price / 安い値段: a low price
Misuse note: 手ごろ is a na-adjective before a noun, so use な. 安い is more direct and focuses only on the amount.

Kana: あさごはんをたべる
Usage note: 朝ご飯 is a common conversational word for breakfast; the food or meal consumed takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 毎朝七時ごろ朝ご飯を食べる。
Example 1 (English): I eat breakfast around seven every morning.
Example 2 (Japanese): 忙しくても朝ご飯を食べてから出かける。
Example 2 (English): Even when I'm busy, I eat breakfast before leaving.
Contrast: 朝食を取る: have breakfast, more formal / 朝ご飯を抜く: skip breakfast
Misuse note: Use を with 食べる. 朝食 is slightly more formal; both refer to the morning meal.

Kana: ていしょくをちゅうもんする
Usage note: 定食 is a fixed set of a main dish and accompaniments; the item ordered takes を with 注文する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 昼は食堂でとんかつ定食を注文した。
Example 1 (English): At lunch, I ordered a pork-cutlet set meal in the cafeteria.
Example 2 (Japanese): 初めての店では日替わり定食を注文することが多い。
Example 2 (English): At a new restaurant, I often order the daily set meal.
Contrast: 定食を頼む: order a set meal, conversational / 単品で注文する: order à la carte
Misuse note: Use を for the ordered item. 頼む is natural in conversation; 注文する is explicit and neutral.

Kana: いんしょくてんでしょくじをする
Meaning: to eat at a food-service establishment
Usage note: 飲食店 is an administrative or category term covering restaurants, cafés, bars, and similar businesses; で marks the place of eating.
Example 1 (Japanese): 駅前の飲食店で食事をした。
Example 1 (English): I ate at a restaurant near the station.
Example 2 (Japanese): この通りには遅くまで飲食店で食事をする人が多い。
Example 2 (English): Many people eat at restaurants on this street late into the evening.
Contrast: 店で食べる: eat at a restaurant / 外食する: eat out
Misuse note: Use で for an action at a place. Choose a more specific venue word when the type of establishment matters.

Kana: めいがらまいをとりよせる
Meaning: to order a branded variety of rice from elsewhere
Usage note: 取り寄せる means having an item sent from another shop, branch, or region; the ordered item takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 産地から二種類の銘柄米を取り寄せた。
Example 1 (English): I ordered two branded rice varieties directly from their producing regions.
Example 2 (Japanese): 食べ比べるために各地の銘柄米を取り寄せる。
Example 2 (English): I order branded rice from several regions to compare them.
Contrast: 米を注文する: order rice / 産地から取り寄せる: order directly from the source
Misuse note: Use を for the item and から for its source. 買う alone does not convey delivery from elsewhere.

Kana: ねだんがたかい
Meaning: for the price to be high; to be expensive
Usage note: Japanese often states that the price is high with 値段が高い; the item can be the topic with は.
Example 1 (Japanese): この店は駅に近いぶん、値段が高い。
Example 1 (English): This shop is more expensive because it is near the station.
Example 2 (Japanese): 品質はいいが、少し値段が高い。
Example 2 (English): The quality is good, but it is a little expensive.
Contrast: 値段が安い: the price is low / 価格が高い: the price is high, more formal
Misuse note: Use が with the property-bearing noun. To say someone raises a price, use 値段を上げる.

Kana: ねだんがたかすぎる
Meaning: for the price to be too high
Usage note: The adjective stem 高 plus すぎる means exceeding an acceptable degree; 値段 takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 便利そうだが、今の予算には値段が高すぎる。
Example 1 (English): It looks useful, but the price is too high for my current budget.
Example 2 (Japanese): この量で千円は値段が高すぎると思う。
Example 2 (English): I think one thousand yen is too expensive for this amount.
Contrast: 値段が高い: the price is high / 予算を超える: exceed the budget
Misuse note: Drop the final い before adding すぎる: 高い becomes 高すぎる.

Kana: かかくがさがる
Usage note: 下がる is intransitive: the price itself decreases and therefore takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 旬になると野菜の価格が下がる。
Example 1 (English): Vegetable prices fall when they come into season.
Example 2 (Japanese): 在庫が増えて商品の価格が下がった。
Example 2 (English): The product's price fell after inventory increased.
Contrast: 価格を下げる: lower a price / 値段が下がる: the price goes down
Misuse note: Use が with 下がる and を with transitive 下げる.

Kana: ぶっかがじょうしょうする
Meaning: for the general cost of living to rise
Usage note: 物価 refers to the overall level of consumer prices, and 上昇する is a formal intransitive pairing.
Example 1 (Japanese): 輸送費の影響で物価が上昇している。
Example 1 (English): The cost of living is rising because of transport costs.
Example 2 (Japanese): 物価が急に上昇すると家計への負担が増える。
Example 2 (English): A sudden rise in the cost of living puts more pressure on household budgets.
Contrast: 物価が上がる: prices rise, everyday wording / 価格が上昇する: a price rises
Misuse note: Use が for the changing price level. 政策などが物価を上昇させる uses the causative form.

Kana: ていしょくをたのむ
Usage note: In restaurants, 頼む is a common conversational alternative to 注文する; the ordered item takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 昼休みに焼き魚定食を頼んだ。
Example 1 (English): I ordered the grilled-fish set at lunch.
Example 2 (Japanese): 迷った末に一番人気の定食を頼んだ。
Example 2 (English): After some hesitation, I ordered the most popular set meal.
Contrast: 定食を注文する: order a set meal / 店員に頼む: ask a staff member
Misuse note: Mark the food with を and the person asked with に. Do not attach に to the menu item.

Kana: でまえをたのむ
Usage note: 出前 is prepared food delivered by a restaurant, and 出前を頼む is the conventional ordering phrase.
Example 1 (Japanese): 雨なので、今夜は寿司の出前を頼む。
Example 1 (English): It's raining, so we'll order sushi for delivery tonight.
Example 2 (Japanese): 忙しい日は近所のそば屋から出前を頼むことがある。
Example 2 (English): On busy days, I sometimes order delivery from the neighborhood soba shop.
Contrast: 料理を配達してもらう: have food delivered / 持ち帰りを頼む: order takeaway
Misuse note: Use を for the service ordered. 店から can mark the source, while 店に can mark the establishment contacted.

Kana: しょくじをおごる
Meaning: to treat someone to a meal
Usage note: おごる means paying for another person's food or drink; the treat takes を and the beneficiary can take に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 昇進のお祝いに先輩が食事をおごってくれた。
Example 1 (English): A senior colleague treated me to a meal to celebrate my promotion.
Example 2 (Japanese): 今日は私がみんなに食事をおごるよ。
Example 2 (English): I'll treat everyone to a meal today.
Contrast: 人に食事をおごる: buy someone a meal / 食事に招く: invite someone to a meal
Misuse note: Use を for what is paid for and に for the person treated. The kanji 奢る is often written in kana in everyday text.

Kana: こうかなしょうひん
Usage note: 高価な is a relatively formal way to describe something carrying a high monetary value.
Example 1 (Japanese): 高価な商品なので、保証内容も確認した。
Example 1 (English): Because it is an expensive product, I also checked the warranty.
Example 2 (Japanese): 店員が高価な商品を鍵付きの棚から出した。
Example 2 (English): The clerk took the expensive item from a locked cabinet.
Contrast: 値段の高い商品: a high-priced product / 高級品: a luxury item
Misuse note: 高価 is a na-adjective before a noun, so use な. 高級 describes class or grade rather than price alone.

Kana: かかくをこうしょうする
Usage note: 交渉する can directly take the issue under negotiation with を; the other party takes と.
Example 1 (Japanese): 複数の商品を買う前に価格を交渉した。
Example 1 (English): I negotiated the price before buying several items.
Example 2 (Japanese): 販売店と配送料を含む価格を交渉する。
Example 2 (English): We negotiate with the dealer over a price that includes delivery.
Contrast: 価格交渉をする: conduct price negotiations / 値段を値切る: haggle the price down
Misuse note: Use を for the issue and と for the counterpart. 値切る is more specifically about asking for a reduction.

Kana: かかくがこうとうする
Usage note: 高騰する describes a steep, conspicuous price rise and is common in news and formal reporting.
Example 1 (Japanese): 不作の影響で野菜の価格が高騰した。
Example 1 (English): Vegetable prices soared after a poor harvest.
Example 2 (Japanese): 需要が集中すると宿泊料金の価格が高騰することがある。
Example 2 (English): Accommodation prices can soar when demand is concentrated.
Contrast: 価格が上昇する: the price rises / 価格が急騰する: the price surges suddenly
Misuse note: The rising price takes が. Use 価格をつり上げる when an actor deliberately drives it higher.

Kana: だとうなかかく
Usage note: 妥当な means supportable or appropriate in light of evidence, conditions, or comparison.
Example 1 (Japanese): 品質を考えれば妥当な価格だと思う。
Example 1 (English): Considering the quality, I think the price is reasonable.
Example 2 (Japanese): 相場を調べて妥当な価格か判断した。
Example 2 (English): I checked the market rate to judge whether the price was reasonable.
Contrast: 適正な価格: a fair or proper price / 手ごろな価格: an affordable price
Misuse note: Use な before a noun. 手ごろ evaluates affordability for the buyer; 妥当 evaluates justification.

Kana: かいてんずしにいく
Meaning: to go to a conveyor-belt sushi restaurant
Usage note: 回転寿司 names the restaurant format as well as the meal experience; the destination takes に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 家族と駅前の回転寿司に行った。
Example 1 (English): I went to a conveyor-belt sushi restaurant near the station with my family.
Example 2 (Japanese): 給料日の夜は回転寿司に行くことが多い。
Example 2 (English): We often go for conveyor-belt sushi on payday night.
Contrast: 寿司屋に行く: go to a sushi restaurant / 回転寿司で食べる: eat at a conveyor-belt sushi place
Misuse note: Use に or へ for the destination and で for the place where eating occurs.

Kana: ねだんをねぎる
Usage note: 値切る means asking a seller to reduce a stated price; the price takes を and the seller can take に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 蚤の市で店主に値段を値切ってみた。
Example 1 (English): I tried haggling with the seller over the price at the flea market.
Example 2 (Japanese): まとめて買う代わりに値段を値切った。
Example 2 (English): I haggled the price down in exchange for buying several items together.
Contrast: 価格を交渉する: negotiate a price / 値下げを頼む: ask for a discount
Misuse note: Use を for the negotiated price. Avoid the behavior at fixed-price shops unless the context clearly permits negotiation.

Kana: かかくがおおはばにあがる
Meaning: for a price to rise substantially
Usage note: 大幅に is an adverb meaning by a large margin; the changing price takes が with intransitive 上がる.
Example 1 (Japanese): 原材料が不足して商品の価格が大幅に上がった。
Example 1 (English): The product's price rose substantially because raw materials were scarce.
Example 2 (Japanese): 繁忙期には航空券の価格が大幅に上がる。
Example 2 (English): Airfare rises substantially during the busy season.
Contrast: 価格が急に上がる: the price rises suddenly / 価格を大幅に上げる: raise the price substantially
Misuse note: Use に to make 大幅 adverbial. Use を and 上げる when naming an actor who raises the price.

Kana: ぶっかがあがる
Meaning: for the cost of living to rise
Usage note: 物価が上がる is the everyday counterpart of the more formal 物価が上昇する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 最近は食料品を中心に物価が上がっている。
Example 1 (English): Recently, the cost of living has been rising, especially for food.
Example 2 (Japanese): 物価が上がると同じ予算で買える物が減る。
Example 2 (English): When the cost of living rises, the same budget buys fewer things.
Contrast: 値段が上がる: an item's price rises / 物価が下がる: the cost of living falls
Misuse note: Use が with intransitive 上がる. For a single product, prefer 値段 or 価格.

Japanese: 商品が軒並み値上がりする
Kana: しょうひんがのきなみねあがりする
Meaning: for products across the board to rise in price
Usage note: 軒並み means nearly every member of a relevant group; 値上がりする describes prices rising.
Example 1 (Japanese): 輸送費が増え、輸入商品が軒並み値上がりした。
Example 1 (English): Transport costs rose, and imported products went up in price across the board.
Example 2 (Japanese): 春から日用品が軒並み値上がりする予定だ。
Example 2 (English): Everyday goods are due to rise in price across the board this spring.
Contrast: 各社が軒並み値上げする: companies raise prices across the board / 多くの商品が値上がりする: many products rise in price
Misuse note: Items whose prices rise take が. 値上げする is transitive and normally names the seller or company as actor.

Kana: かかくがおおはばにさがる
Meaning: for a price to fall substantially
Usage note: The changing price takes が, and 大幅に states that the size of the fall is large.
Example 1 (Japanese): 新モデルの発売後、旧モデルの価格が大幅に下がった。
Example 1 (English): After the new model launched, the old model's price fell substantially.
Example 2 (Japanese): 収穫量が増えれば市場価格が大幅に下がる可能性がある。
Example 2 (English): If the harvest increases, market prices may fall substantially.
Contrast: 価格を大幅に下げる: lower the price substantially / 価格が急落する: the price plunges
Misuse note: Use が with 下がる. Change to を and 下げる when a seller actively cuts the price.

Kana: ぞうすいをたべる
Meaning: to eat rice porridge cooked in seasoned broth
Usage note: 雑炊 is rice simmered in broth, often with egg, vegetables, or leftovers; the food consumed takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 風邪で食欲がないので、温かい雑炊を食べた。
Example 1 (English): I had no appetite because of a cold, so I ate warm rice porridge.
Example 2 (Japanese): 鍋料理の最後に残った汁で雑炊を食べる。
Example 2 (English): At the end of a hot-pot meal, we eat rice porridge made with the remaining broth.
Contrast: おかゆを食べる: eat plain rice porridge / 締めに雑炊を作る: make porridge to finish a hot-pot meal
Misuse note: Use 雑炊 when the seasoned broth and added ingredients matter; use おかゆ for the plainer dish.

Kana: たべほうだいにいく
Meaning: to go out for an all-you-can-eat meal
Usage note: 食べ放題 means eating without a per-item limit under the restaurant's plan; に marks the outing's destination or purpose.
Example 1 (Japanese): 週末に友達と焼肉の食べ放題に行った。
Example 1 (English): I went for all-you-can-eat barbecue with friends at the weekend.
Example 2 (Japanese): 誕生日にホテルの食べ放題に行く予定だ。
Example 2 (English): We're planning to go to a hotel buffet for my birthday.
Contrast: 食べ放題を注文する: order an all-you-can-eat plan / ビュッフェに行く: go to a buffet
Misuse note: Use に with 行く. 食べ放題 and ビュッフェ overlap, but one names a pricing plan and the other a service format.

Kana: みせをよやくする
Meaning: to reserve a restaurant or venue
Usage note: 店を予約する is common shorthand for reserving a table or time slot at that establishment.
Example 1 (Japanese): 記念日の一週間前に創作料理の店を予約した。
Example 1 (English): I booked a creative-cuisine restaurant a week before our anniversary.
Example 2 (Japanese): 人気の店なので早めに予約したほうがいい。
Example 2 (English): It's a popular restaurant, so you should book early.
Contrast: 席を予約する: reserve a seat or table / 店を貸し切る: reserve an entire venue privately
Misuse note: を treats the establishment as what is booked; 店に予約を入れる instead marks it as the recipient of the booking.

Kana: いんしょくてんがたちならぶ
Meaning: for restaurants and bars to line a street
Usage note: 立ち並ぶ describes multiple buildings or shops standing in a row or concentrated along an area.
Example 1 (Japanese): 駅の北口には小さな飲食店が立ち並んでいる。
Example 1 (English): Small restaurants and bars line the street outside the station's north exit.
Example 2 (Japanese): 川沿いに個性的な飲食店が立ち並ぶ。
Example 2 (English): Distinctive restaurants line the riverfront.
Contrast: 店が並ぶ: shops line the street / 飲食店が集まる: restaurants cluster together
Misuse note: Use が with intransitive 立ち並ぶ. 食通り is not an established general word; describe the actual shops or use 飲食店街.

Kana: あまくちのかれー
Usage note: 甘口 labels a mild or sweet flavor category; の links it to the food or drink classified.
Example 1 (Japanese): 辛い物が苦手なので甘口のカレーを注文した。
Example 1 (English): I ordered mild curry because I do not handle spicy food well.
Example 2 (Japanese): 子ども用には甘口のカレーを作る。
Example 2 (English): I make mild curry for the children.
Contrast: 中辛のカレー: medium-hot curry / 辛口のカレー: hot curry
Misuse note: Use の after the noun-like flavor label 甘口. Do not assume 甘い and 甘口 are interchangeable in every product category.

Kana: だいきんをはらいもどす
Usage note: 払い戻す means returning money already paid; the refunded amount or payment takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 品切れになったため、店が注文の代金を払い戻した。
Example 1 (English): The shop refunded the order because the item was out of stock.
Example 2 (Japanese): 返品を受け付けたあとで代金を払い戻します。
Example 2 (English): We will refund the payment after accepting the return.
Contrast: 代金が払い戻される: the payment is refunded / 返金する: issue a refund
Misuse note: Use を when the seller performs the refund. The customer normally receives it with the passive 払い戻される or 返金される.

Kana: なっとうをごはんにかける
Usage note: The topping takes を and the base receiving it takes に with かける.
Example 1 (Japanese): 朝は納豆をご飯にかけて食べる。
Example 1 (English): In the morning, I put natto over rice and eat it.
Example 2 (Japanese): 刻んだねぎを混ぜた納豆をご飯にかけた。
Example 2 (English): I put natto mixed with chopped spring onion over rice.
Contrast: ご飯に卵をかける: put egg over rice / 納豆を混ぜる: stir natto
Misuse note: Keep the direction clear: topping を, food underneath に. Reversing the particles reverses what is put on what.

Kana: あげものをひかえる
Meaning: to cut back on fried food
Usage note: Xを控える means deliberately reducing or avoiding X, often for health, cost, or self-restraint.
Example 1 (Japanese): 胃が疲れているので今週は揚げ物を控えている。
Example 1 (English): My stomach feels worn out, so I am cutting back on fried food this week.
Example 2 (Japanese): 健康診断の前だけでなく普段から揚げ物を控える。
Example 2 (English): I cut back on fried food routinely, not only before health checks.
Contrast: 揚げ物を避ける: avoid fried food / 量を控えめにする: keep the amount modest
Misuse note: Use を for what is reduced. 控えめな揚げ物 would instead describe the food or amount as modest.

Kana: しこみをすませる
Meaning: to finish the advance food preparation
Usage note: 仕込み covers advance preparation of ingredients, stock, dough, and other components; 済ませる marks completing it.
Example 1 (Japanese): 店を開ける前に昼の仕込みを済ませる。
Example 1 (English): We finish the lunch preparation before opening the restaurant.
Example 2 (Japanese): 朝のうちに夕食の仕込みを済ませておいた。
Example 2 (English): I finished the dinner prep in the morning.
Contrast: 仕込みが済む: the preparation is finished / 下ごしらえをする: prepare ingredients
Misuse note: Use を with transitive 済ませる and が with intransitive 済む.

Kana: しめにぞうすいをたのむ
Meaning: to order rice porridge to finish the meal
Usage note: 締めに marks the final dish or action that rounds off a meal or evening; the ordered dish takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 鍋を食べたあと、締めに雑炊を頼んだ。
Example 1 (English): After the hot pot, we ordered rice porridge to finish the meal.
Example 2 (Japanese): 飲んだあとの締めに雑炊を頼む人もいる。
Example 2 (English): Some people order rice porridge to finish an evening of drinking.
Contrast: 締めに麺を入れる: add noodles to finish / 最後に雑炊を食べる: eat porridge at the end
Misuse note: Use に to mark the role 'as the finish.' 締めの一品 is a noun phrase meaning the final dish.

Kana: すききらいなくたべる
Usage note: 好き嫌いなく functions adverbially and means without rejecting foods based on personal likes and dislikes.
Example 1 (Japanese): 子どもには好き嫌いなく食べてほしい。
Example 1 (English): I want my children to eat without being picky.
Example 2 (Japanese): 彼は野菜も魚も好き嫌いなく食べる。
Example 2 (English): He eats vegetables and fish without being picky.
Contrast: 何でも食べる: eat anything / 好き嫌いが多い: be a picky eater
Misuse note: Use なく, not ない, before the verb. Do not use this phrase to dismiss medical or religious dietary needs.

Japanese: 食後に甘味を注文する
Kana: しょくごにかんみをちゅうもんする
Romaji: shokugo ni kanmi o chuumon suru
Meaning: to order a sweet after the meal
Usage note: 食後に marks the timing, while 甘味 is a somewhat traditional or menu-style word for sweets and desserts.
Example 1 (Japanese): 食後にあんみつなどの甘味を注文した。
Example 1 (English): After the meal, I ordered a sweet such as anmitsu.
Example 2 (Japanese): 食後に温かいお茶と甘味を注文する。
Example 2 (English): I order hot tea and a sweet after the meal.
Contrast: デザートを頼む: order dessert / 食後の甘味: an after-meal sweet
Misuse note: Use に for time and を for the ordered item. In casual conversation, デザート may sound more natural.

Kana: たべごたえがある
Meaning: to be substantial and satisfying to eat
Usage note: 食べ応えがある says a food provides a satisfying sense of substance, often because of amount, texture, or density.
Example 1 (Japanese): 厚い肉が入っていて食べ応えがある。
Example 1 (English): The thick pieces of meat make it substantial and satisfying.
Example 2 (Japanese): 豆だけの料理でも調理法しだいで食べ応えがある。
Example 2 (English): Even a bean-only dish can be substantial depending on how it is prepared.
Contrast: 量が多い: be large in quantity / 食べやすい: be easy to eat
Misuse note: Use が with ある. 食べ応えのある is the attributive form before a noun.

Kana: こすぱがいい
Meaning: to offer good value for money
Usage note: コスパ abbreviates cost performance and evaluates value received relative to cost; it is common but informal.
Example 1 (Japanese): このランチは量も味も満足できてコスパがいい。
Example 1 (English): This lunch offers good value: both the portion and flavor are satisfying.
Example 2 (Japanese): 長く使える商品は結果的にコスパがいいこともある。
Example 2 (English): A durable product can turn out to offer good value.
Contrast: 割安だ: be relatively inexpensive / 費用対効果が高い: be cost-effective, formal
Misuse note: Use が with いい. Avoid コスパ in formal reports when 費用対効果 is more appropriate.

Kana: くいだおれをたのしむ
Meaning: to enjoy an extravagant food crawl
Usage note: 食い倒れ evokes spending freely and eating extensively, especially in the expression 京の着倒れ、大阪の食い倒れ.
Example 1 (Japanese): 大阪では店を何軒も回って食い倒れを楽しんだ。
Example 1 (English): In Osaka, we enjoyed an extravagant crawl through several restaurants.
Example 2 (Japanese): 一日かけて商店街の食い倒れを楽しむ計画だ。
Example 2 (English): We plan to spend the day enjoying a food crawl through the shopping district.
Contrast: 食べ歩きを楽しむ: enjoy trying food at different shops / 食べ過ぎる: eat too much
Misuse note: The term can sound promotional or stereotyped; use 食べ歩き for a neutral description of visiting food spots.

Japanese: まとめ買いで節約する
Kana: まとめがいでせつやくする
Meaning: to save money by buying in bulk
Usage note: で marks the means: purchasing several units or a larger quantity at once is used to reduce total cost.
Example 1 (Japanese): 保存できる食品はまとめ買いで節約する。
Example 1 (English): I save money by buying shelf-stable food in bulk.
Example 2 (Japanese): 日用品をまとめ買いで節約できるか単価を比べた。
Example 2 (English): I compared unit prices to see whether buying household goods in bulk would save money.
Contrast: 特売で節約する: save through a sale / まとめて買う: buy several things together
Misuse note: Use で for the method. Check unit price and likely consumption before calling a purchase a saving.

Kana: ねさげをこうしょうする
Usage note: 値下げ is a reduction from the stated price; を marks the matter being negotiated.
Example 1 (Japanese): 展示品に傷があったので値下げを交渉した。
Example 1 (English): The display item was scratched, so I negotiated a discount.
Example 2 (Japanese): 複数台買う条件で値下げを交渉する。
Example 2 (English): We negotiate a discount on condition that we buy several units.
Contrast: 価格を交渉する: negotiate the price / 値下げを頼む: ask for a reduction
Misuse note: Use を for the issue and と for a negotiating counterpart. 打診する is a preliminary feeler, not the negotiation itself.

Japanese: 健康的な食事を心がける
Kana: けんこうてきなしょくじをこころがける
Meaning: to make a conscious effort to eat healthily
Usage note: Xを心がける means keeping X consciously in mind and trying to practice it regularly.
Example 1 (Japanese): 忙しい時期でも健康的な食事を心がけている。
Example 1 (English): Even when work is busy, I make an effort to eat healthily.
Example 2 (Japanese): 外食するときも野菜を含む健康的な食事を心がける。
Example 2 (English): Even when eating out, I try to choose a healthy meal that includes vegetables.
Contrast: 栄養のバランスを意識する: be mindful of nutritional balance / 食生活を改善する: improve one's diet
Misuse note: Use を with the practice kept in mind. 心掛ける is also commonly written 心がける.

Kana: さっぱりしたあじ
Usage note: With food, さっぱりした describes a clean, refreshing taste with little heaviness or lingering richness.
Example 1 (Japanese): 暑い日は酢の物のさっぱりした味がうれしい。
Example 1 (English): On a hot day, the light, clean taste of vinegared food is welcome.
Example 2 (Japanese): レモンを加えるとさっぱりした味になる。
Example 2 (English): Adding lemon gives it a lighter, fresher taste.
Contrast: あっさりした味: a light, mild flavor / こってりした味: a rich, heavy flavor
Misuse note: Use した before a noun. あっさり overlaps, while さっぱり often adds a refreshing after-feel.

Kana: むのうやくのこめ
Usage note: 無農薬の米 is a general descriptive phrase; の links the production claim to rice.
Example 1 (Japanese): 生産者を確認して無農薬の米を選んだ。
Example 1 (English): I checked the producer and chose rice grown without agricultural chemicals.
Example 2 (Japanese): 無農薬の米だという説明だけでなく栽培記録も見た。
Example 2 (English): I looked at the cultivation record rather than relying only on the claim that the rice was pesticide-free.
Contrast: 有機米: organically certified rice / 農薬を減らして作った米: rice grown with reduced pesticide use
Misuse note: Use の after the noun-like modifier. Do not treat 無農薬 and certified 有機 as legally or technically identical.

Japanese: 飲み放題付きのコース
Kana: のみほうだいつきのこーす
Meaning: a set course that includes unlimited drinks
Usage note: X付き means X is included; の connects the resulting modifier to コース.
Example 1 (Japanese): 歓迎会では飲み放題付きのコースを予約した。
Example 1 (English): For the welcome party, we booked a set course with unlimited drinks.
Example 2 (Japanese): 人数が多いので飲み放題付きのコースを頼んだ。
Example 2 (English): Because our group was large, we ordered a course that included unlimited drinks.
Contrast: 食べ放題のコース: an all-you-can-eat plan / 飲み物別のコース: a course with drinks charged separately
Misuse note: Use the suffix 付き directly after what is included. Check the plan's time limit and included menu.

Kana: りょうがおおい
Meaning: for the portion or quantity to be large
Usage note: 量が多い evaluates the amount, with が marking the property-bearing noun.
Example 1 (Japanese): この店の定食は値段のわりに量が多い。
Example 1 (English): This restaurant's set meals are large for the price.
Example 2 (Japanese): 一人では食べ切れないほど量が多い。
Example 2 (English): The portion is so large that one person cannot finish it.
Contrast: 量が少ない: the quantity is small / 大盛りにする: order a larger serving
Misuse note: Use が with 多い. When modifying a noun, Japanese often prefers 量の多い料理 over 多い量の料理.

Kana: げんまいをたべる
Usage note: 玄米 is rice with the bran and germ largely intact; the food consumed takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 昼は白米の代わりに玄米を食べている。
Example 1 (English): At lunch, I eat brown rice instead of white rice.
Example 2 (Japanese): 玄米を食べるときは水加減と炊き方を変える。
Example 2 (English): When I eat brown rice, I adjust the water and cooking method.
Contrast: 白米を食べる: eat white rice / 玄米を炊く: cook brown rice
Misuse note: Use を with 食べる. Any health effect depends on the person's overall diet and circumstances.
