Kana: かぜをよぼうする
Meaning: to reduce the risk of catching or spreading a cold
Usage note: The illness targeted takes を with 予防する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 手洗いと咳エチケットで風邪を予防する。
Example 1 (English): I use handwashing and cough etiquette to reduce the risk of colds.
Example 2 (Japanese): 症状があるときは周囲への感染も考えて風邪を予防する行動を取る。
Example 2 (English): When I have symptoms, I act to reduce transmission to others as well.
Contrast: 感染を防ぐ: prevent infection / 風邪をひく: catch a cold
Misuse note: Use を with 予防する. Follow current public-health guidance and consider people unable to use a particular measure.

Kana: けんしんをうける
Usage note: The examination received takes を with 受ける.
Example 1 (Japanese): 案内された時期に定期検診を受けた。
Example 1 (English): I underwent the regular health screening at the recommended time.
Example 2 (Japanese): 対象と利益・不利益を確認して検診を受ける。
Example 2 (English): I confirm eligibility, benefits, and drawbacks before undergoing screening.
Contrast: 健康診断を受ける: have a health check / 精密検査を受ける: undergo detailed testing
Misuse note: Use を with 受ける. Follow current, individualized screening guidance and arrange follow-up for abnormal results.

Kana: くすりのこうかがあらわれる
Meaning: for a medicine's effect to become apparent
Usage note: の links the medicine and effect, and the effect appearing takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 服用してしばらくすると薬の効果が現れた。
Example 1 (English): The medicine's effect became apparent some time after I took it.
Example 2 (Japanese): 薬の効果が現れなくても自己判断で量を増やさない。
Example 2 (English): Even if the effect does not appear, I do not increase the dose on my own.
Contrast: この薬は効果がある: this medicine is effective / 副作用が現れる: a side effect appears
Misuse note: Use が with 現れる. Follow the product-specific instructions and consult a qualified clinician or pharmacist about response or adverse effects.

Kana: けつあつをはかる
Usage note: The quantity measured takes を with 測る.
Example 1 (Japanese): 説明書どおりの姿勢で血圧を測った。
Example 1 (English): I measured my blood pressure in the posture specified by the instructions.
Example 2 (Japanese): 同じ条件で血圧を測り記録を医療者に見せる。
Example 2 (English): I measure blood pressure under consistent conditions and show the record to a clinician.
Contrast: 体温を測る: measure body temperature / 血圧を記録する: record blood pressure
Misuse note: Use を with 測る. Follow validated-device instructions and seek urgent care for concerning symptoms regardless of a home reading.

Kana: てをあげてあいずする
Meaning: to raise a hand as a signal
Usage note: The body part moved takes を, and the te-form connects the action to signaling.
Example 1 (Japanese): 具合が悪くなり、手を上げて係員に合図した。
Example 1 (English): I began to feel ill and raised my hand to signal the attendant.
Example 2 (Japanese): 声が出しにくいときは手を上げて合図する。
Example 2 (English): When speaking is difficult, I raise my hand to signal.
Contrast: 声を出して助けを求める: call out for help / 手を振って知らせる: wave to alert someone
Misuse note: Use を with 上げる. Establish accessible alternative signals in care, sport, work, and emergency settings.

Kana: しょうじょうがかくにんされる
Meaning: for a symptom to be observed or confirmed
Usage note: The observed symptom takes が in the passive construction.
Example 1 (Japanese): 診察で皮膚の症状が確認された。
Example 1 (English): A skin symptom was observed during the examination.
Example 2 (Japanese): 症状が確認されても検査結果と合わせて判断する。
Example 2 (English): Even when a symptom is observed, it is interpreted together with test results.
Contrast: 症状を確認する: check a symptom / 病気が診断される: a disease is diagnosed
Misuse note: Use が in the passive. Keep observation, test result, differential assessment, and diagnosis distinct.

Kana: てがるにつくれるしょくじ
Meaning: a meal that is easy to prepare
Usage note: 手軽に modifies 作れる and means requiring relatively little effort, time, skill, or equipment.
Example 1 (Japanese): 疲れた日でも手軽に作れる食事を選んだ。
Example 1 (English): I chose a meal that was easy to prepare even on a tiring day.
Example 2 (Japanese): 材料と栄養表示を見て手軽に作れる食事を選ぶ。
Example 2 (English): I check the ingredients and nutrition label when choosing an easy-to-prepare meal.
Contrast: 簡単に作れる料理: a dish that is easy to make / 調理済みの食事: a prepared meal
Misuse note: Use に to make 手軽 adverbial before the verb. Match food to individual allergies, swallowing needs, and medical advice.

Japanese: 体のバランスが崩れる
Kana: からだのばらんすがくずれる
Usage note: の links the body and balance, and the state that breaks down takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 急に立ち上がると体のバランスが崩れた。
Example 1 (English): I lost my balance when I stood up suddenly.
Example 2 (Japanese): 突然体のバランスが崩れて立てないときは助けを求める。
Example 2 (English): If I suddenly lose balance and cannot stand, I seek help.
Contrast: バランスを崩す: lose one's balance / ふらつく: feel or move unsteadily
Misuse note: Use が with intransitive 崩れる. Sudden severe unsteadiness can be an emergency warning sign.

Kana: かんぶをかばってあるく
Meaning: to walk while protecting an injured area
Usage note: The injured part protected takes を, and the te-form links the protective action to walking.
Example 1 (Japanese): 足首を痛め、患部をかばって歩いていた。
Example 1 (English): I had hurt my ankle and was walking while favoring the injured area.
Example 2 (Japanese): 患部をかばって歩く状態が続くので医療機関に相談した。
Example 2 (English): I sought medical advice because I kept walking while favoring the injured area.
Contrast: 足を引きずって歩く: walk with a limp / 患部を動かさない: keep the injured part still
Misuse note: Use を with かばう. Significant injury, inability to bear weight, deformity, or severe pain needs appropriate assessment.

Japanese: 検査結果を本人に渡す
Kana: けんさけっかをほんにんにわたす
Romaji: kensa kekka o honnin ni watasu
Meaning: to give test results to the person concerned
Usage note: The document transferred takes を and the recipient takes に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 本人確認をしてから検査結果を本人に渡した。
Example 1 (English): I verified the person's identity before giving them the test results.
Example 2 (Japanese): 封筒に入れて検査結果を本人に渡す。
Example 2 (English): I place the test results in an envelope and give them to the person concerned.
Contrast: 検査結果を説明する: explain test results / 資料を全員に配る: distribute materials to everyone
Misuse note: Use を for the results and に for the recipient. Follow current identity, consent, proxy, privacy, and record-access rules.

Kana: けんこうしこうがたかまる
Meaning: for interest in health-oriented choices to grow
Usage note: 健康志向 refers to a tendency to prioritize perceived health; the tendency increasing takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 利用者の間で健康志向が高まっている。
Example 1 (English): Interest in health-oriented choices is growing among users.
Example 2 (Japanese): 健康志向が高まっても広告の根拠を確認する。
Example 2 (English): Even as health interest grows, I check the evidence behind advertising claims.
Contrast: 健康志向を高める: increase health consciousness / 健康への関心が高まる: interest in health grows
Misuse note: Use が with intransitive 高まる. Do not turn a market trend into a medical recommendation.

Kana: いやくひんをとりあつかう
Meaning: to handle or deal in medicines
Usage note: The goods handled take を with 取り扱う; the verb can cover storage, sale, supply, transport, and administration depending on context.
Example 1 (Japanese): 許可を受けた施設で医薬品を取り扱っている。
Example 1 (English): The licensed facility handles medicines.
Example 2 (Japanese): 温度と記録の要件に従って医薬品を取り扱う。
Example 2 (English): We handle medicines according to temperature and recordkeeping requirements.
Contrast: 医薬品を販売する: sell medicines / 薬を保管する: store medicine
Misuse note: Use を with 取り扱う. Verify current medicine-specific and jurisdiction-specific licensing, storage, labeling, and traceability rules.

Kana: こっせつのうたがいがある
Meaning: for a fracture to be suspected
Usage note: Xの疑いがある marks a possibility requiring assessment, not a confirmed diagnosis.
Example 1 (Japanese): 強い痛みと変形があり骨折の疑いがある。
Example 1 (English): The severe pain and deformity raise suspicion of a fracture.
Example 2 (Japanese): 骨折の疑いがある部位を無理に動かさず助けを求める。
Example 2 (English): I avoid moving the area unnecessarily and seek help when a fracture is suspected.
Contrast: 骨折と診断される: be diagnosed with a fracture / 骨折を疑う: suspect a fracture
Misuse note: Use の before 疑い and が with ある. Deformity, severe pain, open injury, loss of circulation or sensation, or major trauma needs urgent assessment.

Kana: かたをゆっくりまわす
Usage note: The body part moved takes を and ゆっくり describes manner.
Example 1 (Japanese): 痛みのない範囲で肩をゆっくり回した。
Example 1 (English): I rolled my shoulders slowly within a pain-free range.
Example 2 (Japanese): 専門家の指示に従って肩をゆっくり回す。
Example 2 (English): I roll my shoulders slowly according to professional instructions.
Contrast: 肩を動かす: move the shoulder / 腕を回す: circle one's arm
Misuse note: Use を with 回す. Stop and seek appropriate advice for sharp pain, weakness, numbness, trauma, or worsening symptoms.

Kana: ちりょうをたんとうする
Usage note: The work assigned takes を with 担当する; the responsible person can take が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 専門の医師が治療を担当している。
Example 1 (English): A specialist physician is responsible for the treatment.
Example 2 (Japanese): 複数の職種が役割を分けて治療を担当する。
Example 2 (English): Several professions divide responsibilities for treatment.
Contrast: 診療を担当する: be responsible for clinical care / 治療チームに加わる: join the treatment team
Misuse note: Use を with 担当する. Titles, scope of practice, consent, and responsibility depend on the actual care setting.

Kana: くしんのすえにかいふくする
Romaji: kushin no sue ni kaifuku suru
Meaning: to recover after great difficulty and effort
Usage note: Xの末に marks the result reached after a prolonged process; 苦心 stresses effort and hardship.
Example 1 (Japanese): 長い治療と支援を受け、苦心の末に回復した。
Example 1 (English): After prolonged treatment and support, the person recovered with great difficulty.
Example 2 (Japanese): 苦心の末に回復したという表現を本人の経験に合わせて使う。
Example 2 (English): I use the phrase 'recovered after great difficulty' only when it matches the person's experience.
Contrast: 治療の末に回復する: recover after treatment / 徐々に回復する: recover gradually
Misuse note: Use の末に as a unit. Avoid turning illness outcomes into moral judgments about effort or attitude.

Kana: たいおんをはかる
Usage note: The quantity measured takes を with 測る.
Example 1 (Japanese): 説明書を読んで同じ方法で体温を測った。
Example 1 (English): I read the instructions and measured my temperature using the same method.
Example 2 (Japanese): 症状と時刻も一緒に記録して体温を測る。
Example 2 (English): I measure my temperature and record the symptoms and time as well.
Contrast: 熱を測る: take one's temperature, conversational / 体温を記録する: record body temperature
Misuse note: Use を with 測る. Follow the device instructions and seek care based on the overall condition, not one number alone.

Kana: しょうじょうのあっかをふせぐ
Usage note: の links the symptoms and worsening, and the event prevented takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 医療者の指示に従って症状の悪化を防いだ。
Example 1 (English): I followed the clinician's instructions to prevent the symptoms from worsening.
Example 2 (Japanese): 急な変化を記録しながら症状の悪化を防ぐ方法を相談する。
Example 2 (English): I record sudden changes and ask how to prevent the symptoms from worsening.
Contrast: 症状が悪化する: symptoms worsen / 重症化を防ぐ: prevent progression to severe disease
Misuse note: Use を with 防ぐ. Emergency warning signs require prompt local emergency guidance rather than routine prevention steps.

Kana: からだにきをつける
Meaning: to take care of one's health
Usage note: Xに気をつける is an idiom meaning to pay attention or take care regarding X.
Example 1 (Japanese): 忙しい時期だからこそ体に気をつけている。
Example 1 (English): I make an extra effort to take care of my health during busy periods.
Example 2 (Japanese): 『体に気をつけて』だけでなく必要な支援も尋ねる。
Example 2 (English): Rather than only saying 'take care,' I also ask what support is needed.
Contrast: 健康に気をつける: take care of one's health / お体に気をつけてください: please take care, polite
Misuse note: Use に for the concern and を in the fixed noun 気を. Add specific, evidence-based guidance only when qualified and appropriate.

Kana: ゆっくりやすむ
Meaning: to rest properly and without rushing
Usage note: ゆっくり adverbially describes unhurried, ample rest.
Example 1 (Japanese): 疲れを感じたので家でゆっくり休んだ。
Example 1 (English): I felt tired, so I rested properly at home.
Example 2 (Japanese): ゆっくり休んでも強い症状が続くなら相談する。
Example 2 (English): If severe symptoms continue despite rest, I seek advice.
Contrast: 十分に休む: rest adequately / 安静にする: rest and avoid exertion, medical/formal
Misuse note: Use ゆっくり directly without に. Follow urgent guidance for severe, sudden, or worsening symptoms.

Kana: はっしょうからはんとしがたつ
Meaning: for six months to have passed since symptom onset
Usage note: から marks the starting event, and the elapsed period takes が with 経つ.
Example 1 (Japanese): 最初の症状が出た発症から半年が経った。
Example 1 (English): Six months have passed since the first symptoms appeared.
Example 2 (Japanese): 記録を確認して発症から半年が経つ時点を数えた。
Example 2 (English): I checked the records to calculate the point six months after onset.
Contrast: 診断から半年が経つ: six months pass since diagnosis / 発病してから半年が経つ: six months pass since becoming ill
Misuse note: Use から for the starting point. Define how onset is determined when dates affect research, benefits, or treatment.

Japanese: 手すりをしっかり握る
Kana: てすりをしっかりにぎる
Usage note: The object gripped takes を and しっかり describes a secure manner.
Example 1 (Japanese): 階段では手すりをしっかり握った。
Example 1 (English): I held the handrail firmly on the stairs.
Example 2 (Japanese): 足元を確認しながら手すりをしっかり握る。
Example 2 (English): I hold the handrail firmly while watching my footing.
Contrast: 手すりにつかまる: hold on to a handrail / 手すりから手を離す: let go of the rail
Misuse note: Use を with 握る and に with つかまる. Provide appropriate assistance and accessible alternatives.

Kana: きのうのかいふくをめざす
Usage note: の links the function and recovery, and the target aimed for takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 本人の目標に合わせて手の機能の回復を目指した。
Example 1 (English): We aimed to restore hand function in line with the person's goals.
Example 2 (Japanese): 医療者と相談しながら無理なく機能の回復を目指す。
Example 2 (English): I work toward functional recovery at a manageable pace with clinical guidance.
Contrast: 機能を改善する: improve function / 生活の質を高める: improve quality of life
Misuse note: Use を with 目指す. Set individualized goals without promising a specific recovery outcome.

Kana: さむさをかんじる
Usage note: The sensation perceived takes を with 感じる.
Example 1 (Japanese): 部屋に入っても強い寒さを感じた。
Example 1 (English): I still felt intensely cold after entering the room.
Example 2 (Japanese): 震えを伴う寒さを感じるときは体温と他の症状も確認する。
Example 2 (English): When I feel cold with shivering, I also check my temperature and other symptoms.
Contrast: 寒いと感じる: feel that it is cold / 体が冷える: become chilled
Misuse note: Use を with 感じる. Seek appropriate help for severe exposure, confusion, breathing difficulty, or other alarming symptoms.

Kana: ぜんしんのちからをこめる
Meaning: to put one's whole-body strength into an action
Usage note: 力を込める means deliberately applying force; 全身の specifies its source or extent.
Example 1 (Japanese): 重い物を動かそうとして全身の力を込めた。
Example 1 (English): I put my whole-body strength into trying to move the heavy object.
Example 2 (Japanese): 全身の力を込める前に安全な方法と補助具を確認する。
Example 2 (English): Before using whole-body force, I check a safe method and assistive equipment.
Contrast: 力を入れる: exert force / 渾身の力を込める: put in every ounce of strength, literary
Misuse note: Use を with 込める. Do not lift beyond ability; follow trained manual-handling guidance.

Kana: しかいがかすむ
Meaning: for one's vision to become blurred or hazy
Usage note: The visual field undergoing the change takes が with かすむ.
Example 1 (Japanese): 突然視界がかすみ、文字が読みにくくなった。
Example 1 (English): My vision suddenly became blurred, and the text was hard to read.
Example 2 (Japanese): 突然視界がかすむ場合は運転をやめて助けを求める。
Example 2 (English): If my vision suddenly blurs, I stop driving and seek help.
Contrast: 目がかすむ: have blurred vision / 視界が狭くなる: one's visual field narrows
Misuse note: Use が with かすむ. Sudden vision change, double vision, weakness, speech trouble, or severe headache can require emergency care.

Kana: いたみにたえる
Usage note: The hardship endured takes に with 耐える.
Example 1 (Japanese): 助けが来るまで動かず強い痛みに耐えた。
Example 1 (English): I stayed still and endured severe pain until help arrived.
Example 2 (Japanese): 強い痛みに耐え続けず医療機関に相談する。
Example 2 (English): I seek medical advice rather than continuing to endure severe pain.
Contrast: 痛みを我慢する: put up with pain / 痛みを和らげる: ease pain
Misuse note: Use に with 耐える. Sudden or severe pain and pain with emergency warning signs require prompt assessment.

Kana: きんきゅうしゅじゅつをうける
Usage note: The procedure received takes を with 受ける.
Example 1 (Japanese): 検査のあと医師の説明を受けて緊急手術を受けた。
Example 1 (English): After testing and an explanation from the physician, the patient underwent emergency surgery.
Example 2 (Japanese): 緊急手術を受ける前に可能な範囲で本人確認と説明を行う。
Example 2 (English): Before emergency surgery, identity and explanation are addressed as far as circumstances allow.
Contrast: 手術を受ける: undergo surgery / 緊急処置を受ける: receive emergency treatment
Misuse note: Use を with 受ける. Clinical decisions and consent follow the actual emergency, law, capacity, and professional standards.

Japanese: 左右の見え方を比べる
Kana: さゆうのみえかたをくらべる
Meaning: to compare vision between the two eyes
Usage note: の links left and right with the manner of seeing, and the compared item takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 片目ずつ隠して左右の見え方を比べた。
Example 1 (English): I covered one eye at a time and compared how each eye saw.
Example 2 (Japanese): 急に左右の見え方が変わったら比べるだけで済ませず助けを求める。
Example 2 (English): If vision suddenly differs between the eyes, I seek help rather than stopping at a comparison.
Contrast: 視力を測る: measure visual acuity / 見え方の違いに気づく: notice a difference in vision
Misuse note: Use を with 比べる. Sudden loss, narrowing, double vision, or neurological symptoms can be an emergency.

Kana: つかのまのきゅうそくをとる
Usage note: 束の間の means lasting only a short while; the rest taken takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 長い介護の合間に束の間の休息を取った。
Example 1 (English): I took a brief respite during a long period of caregiving.
Example 2 (Japanese): 束の間の休息を取るだけでなく継続的な支援も利用する。
Example 2 (English): I use ongoing support rather than relying only on brief respites.
Contrast: 短い休憩を取る: take a short break / 十分な休息を取る: get adequate rest
Misuse note: Use の before 休息 and を with 取る. In ordinary prose, 短い休憩 is clearer.

Kana: のうきをまえだおしする
Meaning: to move a delivery deadline earlier
Usage note: The deadline moved earlier takes を with 前倒しする.
Example 1 (Japanese): 顧客と合意して納期を一週間前倒しした。
Example 1 (English): With the customer's agreement, we moved the delivery deadline forward by one week.
Example 2 (Japanese): 必要な人員を確認してから納期を前倒しする。
Example 2 (English): We check the required staffing before moving the deadline forward.
Contrast: 納期を延期する: postpone a deadline / 作業を前倒しする: move work forward
Misuse note: Use を with 前倒しする. Record agreement, revised scope, dependencies, and consequences.

Kana: よていがはくしになる
Meaning: for a plan to be canceled or reset completely
Usage note: 白紙になる is an idiom meaning returning to an undecided state; the plan takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 会場が使えなくなり来月の予定が白紙になった。
Example 1 (English): Next month's plan was scrapped when the venue became unavailable.
Example 2 (Japanese): 予定が白紙になった理由と今後の連絡方法を伝える。
Example 2 (English): We explain why the plan was reset and how updates will be communicated.
Contrast: 予定が中止になる: the event is canceled / 計画を白紙に戻す: return a plan to square one
Misuse note: Use が with なる and を with the transitive 戻す pattern. Avoid the phrase when the plan is only postponed.

Kana: きそくをまもる
Usage note: 守る conventionally pairs with rules and promises to mean observing them.
Example 1 (Japanese): 施設を利用するときは安全の規則を守る。
Example 1 (English): I follow the safety rules when using the facility.
Example 2 (Japanese): 規則を守るだけでなく目的と例外も確認する。
Example 2 (English): I check the purpose and exceptions rather than merely following the rule.
Contrast: 規則に従う: comply with a rule / 規則を破る: break a rule
Misuse note: Use を with 守る. Verify the rule's current text, scope, authority, and accommodation or appeal process.

Kana: よていをつたえる
Meaning: to tell someone one's plans or schedule
Usage note: The information conveyed takes を and the recipient can take に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 家族に帰宅の予定を伝えた。
Example 1 (English): I told my family when I expected to return home.
Example 2 (Japanese): 未確定の部分を明示して予定を伝える。
Example 2 (English): I state what remains tentative when sharing the plan.
Contrast: 予定を共有する: share a schedule / 変更を知らせる: notify someone of a change
Misuse note: Use を for the information and に for the recipient. Mark tentative times clearly.

Kana: けっかをけいさいする
Meaning: to publish results in a document or online
Usage note: The content published takes を and the publication location can take に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 方法と対象者数を添えて調査結果をウェブサイトに掲載した。
Example 1 (English): We published the survey results on the website with the method and sample size.
Example 2 (Japanese): 個人を特定できない形で結果を掲載する。
Example 2 (English): We publish the results in a form that does not identify individuals.
Contrast: 結果を公表する: make results public / 記事を掲載する: publish an article
Misuse note: Use を for the content and に for the medium. Verify privacy, consent, source, copyright, and correction procedures.

Kana: てじゅんをしゅうちする
Meaning: to make a procedure known to everyone concerned
Usage note: The information disseminated takes を; 周知する implies reaching the relevant population broadly.
Example 1 (Japanese): 変更点を強調して新しい手順を周知した。
Example 1 (English): We communicated the new procedure, highlighting what had changed.
Example 2 (Japanese): 理解度を確認しながら手順を周知する。
Example 2 (English): We communicate the procedure and check understanding.
Contrast: 手順を共有する: share a procedure / 変更を通知する: notify people of a change
Misuse note: Use を with 周知する. Define the audience, channels, accessible formats, effective date, and acknowledgement method.

Kana: きやくをてきようする
Usage note: The rule set applied takes を, and the case receiving it can take に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 申込日当時の規約を契約に適用した。
Example 1 (English): We applied the terms in effect on the application date to the contract.
Example 2 (Japanese): 規約を適用する前に版と同意記録を確認する。
Example 2 (English): Before applying the terms, we check the version and consent record.
Contrast: 規約が適用される: the terms apply / 法律を適用する: apply a law
Misuse note: Use を with transitive 適用する. Verify current law, version, notice, consent, hierarchy, and consumer protections.

Kana: よていをへんこうする
Meaning: to change a plan or schedule
Usage note: The plan altered takes を with 変更する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 天候のため午後の予定を変更した。
Example 1 (English): We changed the afternoon plan because of the weather.
Example 2 (Japanese): 関係者に連絡してから予定を変更する。
Example 2 (English): I contact those affected before changing the plan.
Contrast: 予定が変更になる: the schedule is changed / 予定を取り消す: cancel a plan
Misuse note: Use を with the transitive verb. Confirm linked bookings, deadlines, and responsibilities.

Kana: りょうきんをかいていする
Meaning: to revise a fee or tariff
Usage note: The formally revised fee takes を with 改定する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 原価と利用者への影響を検討して料金を改定した。
Example 1 (English): We revised the fee after considering costs and the effect on users.
Example 2 (Japanese): 適用日と解約条件を知らせて料金を改定する。
Example 2 (English): We state the effective date and cancellation terms when revising the fee.
Contrast: 料金を変更する: change a fee / 価格を改定する: revise a price
Misuse note: Use を with 改定する. Verify current approval, filing, contract, notice, and consumer-protection requirements.

Kana: にっていをちょうせいする
Meaning: to coordinate or adjust a schedule
Usage note: The schedule coordinated takes を; counterparts may take と.
Example 1 (Japanese): 参加者の都合を聞いて会議の日程を調整した。
Example 1 (English): We coordinated the meeting schedule after asking about participants' availability.
Example 2 (Japanese): 時差と休業日を考慮して日程を調整する。
Example 2 (English): We coordinate the schedule while considering time zones and holidays.
Contrast: 日程を変更する: change the schedule / 予定をすり合わせる: align schedules
Misuse note: Use を with 調整する. Record the confirmed zone, date, time, participants, and deadline for response.

Kana: けいやくをこうしんする
Usage note: The agreement renewed takes を with 更新する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 条件と期間を確認して契約を更新した。
Example 1 (English): We renewed the contract after checking its terms and duration.
Example 2 (Japanese): 自動更新の期限前に契約を更新するか判断する。
Example 2 (English): We decide whether to renew before the automatic-renewal deadline.
Contrast: 契約が更新される: the contract is renewed / 契約を延長する: extend a contract
Misuse note: Use を with 更新する. Verify current terms, notice, authority, renewal mechanism, cancellation, and applicable law.

Kana: けっかをこうひょうする
Usage note: The information made public takes を with 公表する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 集計方法を説明して選考結果を公表した。
Example 1 (English): We announced the selection results and explained the tabulation method.
Example 2 (Japanese): 異議申立ての方法も示して結果を公表する。
Example 2 (English): We publish the results together with the appeal procedure.
Contrast: 結果を掲載する: publish results in a medium / 結果を発表する: announce results
Misuse note: Use を with 公表する. State authority, method, date, scope, privacy controls, and correction or appeal route.

Kana: きそくをじゅんしゅする
Usage note: The rule observed takes を; 遵守する is formal and common in legal, compliance, and organizational writing.
Example 1 (Japanese): 担当者は安全に関する規則を遵守した。
Example 1 (English): The person in charge complied with the safety rules.
Example 2 (Japanese): 最新版を確認して規則を遵守する。
Example 2 (English): We check the latest version and comply with the rules.
Contrast: 規則を守る: follow rules, everyday wording / 法令を遵守する: comply with laws and regulations
Misuse note: Use を with 遵守する. Verify authority, version, scope, exceptions, and conflict with higher norms.

Japanese: 公金の使途を公開する
Kana: こうきんのしとをこうかいする
Romaji: koukin no shito o koukai suru
Meaning: to disclose how public money is used
Usage note: の links public funds and their use, and the information disclosed takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 自治体は事業ごとに公金の使途を公開した。
Example 1 (English): The municipality disclosed how public money was used for each program.
Example 2 (Japanese): 機械で読める形式でも公金の使途を公開する。
Example 2 (English): We disclose public spending in a machine-readable format as well.
Contrast: 支出内訳を公表する: publish an expenditure breakdown / 公金を横領する: embezzle public money
Misuse note: Use を with 公開する. Protect legitimately confidential data while providing scope, period, definitions, and correction history.

Kana: かんげいかいをもよおす
Usage note: The event held takes を with 催す; the verb is somewhat formal.
Example 1 (Japanese): 新しい参加者の希望を聞いて歓迎会を催した。
Example 1 (English): We held a welcome gathering after asking what the new participants wanted.
Example 2 (Japanese): 参加しない選択も示したうえで歓迎会を催す。
Example 2 (English): We make nonparticipation an explicit option when holding the welcome event.
Contrast: 歓迎会を開く: hold a welcome party / 歓迎会に参加する: attend a welcome gathering
Misuse note: Use を with 催す. Provide accessible, inclusive, voluntary formats and clarify costs and working-time treatment.

Kana: しょうらいぞうをえがく
Usage note: 描く metaphorically means forming a concrete picture of a desired future.
Example 1 (Japanese): 地域の人と十年後の将来像を描いた。
Example 1 (English): We envisioned the community ten years from now with local residents.
Example 2 (Japanese): 複数の可能性を比べながら将来像を描く。
Example 2 (English): We envision the future while comparing several possibilities.
Contrast: 将来の夢を描く: dream about the future / 将来計画を立てる: make a future plan
Misuse note: Use を with 描く. Identify participants, assumptions, conflicts, resources, and measures that connect vision to action.

Kana: しこうきじつをさだめる
Usage note: The date formally fixed takes を with 定める.
Example 1 (Japanese): 準備期間を考慮して新制度の施行期日を定めた。
Example 1 (English): The effective date of the new system was set after considering preparation time.
Example 2 (Japanese): 経過措置と合わせて施行期日を定める。
Example 2 (English): We set the effective date together with transitional measures.
Contrast: 施行期日が定まる: the effective date is settled / 施行日を延期する: postpone the effective date
Misuse note: Use を with 定める. Verify the enacted text, supplementary provisions, amendments, authority, and current e-Gov version.

Kana: ぎょうせいがたいおうする
Meaning: for a public authority to respond
Usage note: The responding institution takes が, while the matter addressed can take に.
Example 1 (Japanese): 住民からの相談に行政が対応した。
Example 1 (English): The public authority responded to inquiries from residents.
Example 2 (Japanese): 担当部署を明らかにして行政が対応する。
Example 2 (English): The public authority responds and identifies the responsible department.
Contrast: 行政の対応が遅い: the administrative response is slow / 自治体が対応する: the local government responds
Misuse note: Use が with 対応する and に for the issue. Distinguish acknowledgement, investigation, decision, remedy, and completion.

Kana: てんじかいをかいさいする
Meaning: to hold an exhibition or trade show
Usage note: The event held takes を with 開催する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 地域の作家を紹介する展示会を開催した。
Example 1 (English): We held an exhibition introducing local artists.
Example 2 (Japanese): 作品の許諾と返却条件を決めて展示会を開催する。
Example 2 (English): We obtain permissions and set return conditions before holding the exhibition.
Contrast: 展示会が開催される: an exhibition is held / 作品を展示する: display works
Misuse note: Use を with the transitive verb. Record rights, loans, access, safety, sales, and cancellation responsibilities.

Japanese: 土壇場で計画を変更する
Kana: どたんばでけいかくをへんこうする
Romaji: dotanba de keikaku o henkou suru
Meaning: to change a plan at the last moment
Usage note: 土壇場で means at the final, critical moment; the plan altered takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 会場の故障が分かり土壇場で計画を変更した。
Example 1 (English): We changed the plan at the last moment after discovering a venue failure.
Example 2 (Japanese): 土壇場で計画を変更した理由と影響を記録する。
Example 2 (English): We record why the plan changed at the last moment and what it affected.
Contrast: 直前に予定を変更する: change plans immediately beforehand / 土壇場で逆転する: reverse the outcome at the last moment
Misuse note: Use で after 土壇場. Notify affected people and preserve safety, consent, and refund rights.

Kana: ゆうこうきげんをかくにんする
Meaning: to check an expiration or validity date
Usage note: The date or period checked takes を; 有効期限 identifies when validity ends.
Example 1 (Japanese): 利用する前に証明書の有効期限を確認した。
Example 1 (English): I checked the document's expiration date before using it.
Example 2 (Japanese): 年月日と時刻まで含めて有効期限を確認する。
Example 2 (English): I check the validity deadline down to the date and time.
Contrast: 使用期限を確認する: check a use-by date / 契約期間を確認する: check a contract term
Misuse note: Use を with 確認する. Check the issuer's current record when status can change independently of the printed date.

Kana: あかるいみらいをえがく
Usage note: 明るい metaphorically means hopeful or promising, and the envisioned future takes を.
Example 1 (Japanese): 課題を隠さずに明るい未来を描いた。
Example 1 (English): We envisioned a hopeful future without hiding the problems.
Example 2 (Japanese): 実行できる小さな目標から明るい未来を描く。
Example 2 (English): We envision a hopeful future starting with small actionable goals.
Contrast: 未来を信じる: believe in the future / 将来像を描く: envision a future state
Misuse note: Use を with 描く. Connect aspiration to responsible action and measurable outcomes.

Kana: きそくにしたがう
Usage note: The rule followed takes に with 従う.
Example 1 (Japanese): 利用者は施設の安全規則に従った。
Example 1 (English): Users followed the facility's safety rules.
Example 2 (Japanese): 規則に従う前に適用範囲と最新版を確認する。
Example 2 (English): Before following a rule, I check its scope and current version.
Contrast: 規則を守る: observe a rule / 指示に従う: follow an instruction
Misuse note: Use に with 従う. Use lawful reporting, accommodation, and appeal routes when a rule creates harm or conflict.

Kana: ちいきしゃかいにこうけんする
Meaning: to contribute to the local community
Usage note: The beneficiary takes に with 貢献する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 住民の希望を聞いて地域社会に貢献する活動を始めた。
Example 1 (English): We began an activity that contributed to the local community after hearing residents' wishes.
Example 2 (Japanese): 成果と負担を住民と検証して地域社会に貢献する。
Example 2 (English): We assess benefits and burdens with residents while contributing to the community.
Contrast: 地域に役立つ: benefit the community / 地域活動に参加する: participate in community activities
Misuse note: Use に with 貢献する. Define community, consent, outcome, and who bears the cost.

Kana: よろんがせいじをうごかす
Meaning: for public opinion to influence politics
Usage note: The influencing force takes が and the system affected takes を with 動かす.
Example 1 (Japanese): 大規模な抗議をきっかけに世論が政治を動かした。
Example 1 (English): Public opinion influenced politics after large protests.
Example 2 (Japanese): 一つの調査だけで世論が政治を動かしたと断定しない。
Example 2 (English): We do not conclude from one survey that public opinion drove political change.
Contrast: 世論が変わる: public opinion changes / 政治に影響を与える: influence politics
Misuse note: Use が for the influence and を for the affected domain. Cite dated, representative evidence and separate correlation from causation.

Japanese: パスポートを更新する
Kana: ぱすぽーとをこうしんする
Usage note: The document being renewed takes を with 更新する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 有効期限を確かめて早めにパスポートを更新した。
Example 1 (English): I checked the expiration date and renewed my passport early.
Example 2 (Japanese): 渡航日が決まる前にパスポートを更新する。
Example 2 (English): I will renew my passport before fixing my travel date.
Contrast: パスポートを申請する: apply for a passport / 情報を更新する: update information
Misuse note: Use を for the item renewed. Check the current official procedure rather than treating the example as procedural advice.

Kana: しじょうにかいにゅうする
Usage note: The sphere entered or affected takes に with 介入する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 政府が急激な混乱を抑えるため市場に介入した。
Example 1 (English): The government intervened in the market to curb sudden disruption.
Example 2 (Japanese): 市場に介入する前後の指標を分けて検証する。
Example 2 (English): We assess the indicators before and after intervening in the market separately.
Contrast: 市場を規制する: regulate a market / 取引に介入する: intervene in a transaction
Misuse note: Use に, not を, with 介入する. State the actor, instrument, date, and observed result when making a policy claim.

Kana: ちいきのひとびととこうりゅうする
Romaji: chiiki no hitobito to kouryuu suru
Meaning: to interact with people in the local community
Usage note: The people one interacts with take と; 交流する suggests reciprocal contact.
Example 1 (Japanese): 祭りの準備を通して地域の人々と交流した。
Example 1 (English): I interacted with people in the local community while preparing for the festival.
Example 2 (Japanese): 短い訪問でも地域の人々と交流する機会を大切にした。
Example 2 (English): Even on a short visit, I valued opportunities to interact with local people.
Contrast: 地域の人々に会う: meet local people / 住民同士が交流する: residents interact with one another
Misuse note: Use と for the other participants. Prefer a specific activity over vague claims of cultural exchange.

Kana: れいがいをもうける
Usage note: The exception created takes を with 設ける.
Example 1 (Japanese): 安全上の理由がある場合に限り例外を設けた。
Example 1 (English): We provided an exception only when there was a safety reason.
Example 2 (Japanese): 例外を設けるなら適用条件を文書にする。
Example 2 (English): If we provide an exception, we document its conditions.
Contrast: 例外を認める: allow an exception / 規則に例外はない: there is no exception to the rule
Misuse note: Use を with 設ける. Do not imply that a stated exception is lawful or fair without checking the governing rule.

Japanese: 地域の催しに参加する
Kana: ちいきのもよおしにさんかする
Romaji: chiiki no moyooshi ni sanka suru
Meaning: to take part in a local event
Usage note: The event joined takes に with 参加する; 催し is a somewhat formal word for an event or program.
Example 1 (Japanese): 転入した翌月に地域の催しに参加した。
Example 1 (English): I took part in a local event the month after moving in.
Example 2 (Japanese): 案内の参加条件を確認して地域の催しに参加する。
Example 2 (English): I check the participation conditions in the notice before joining the local event.
Contrast: 催しを開く: hold an event / 地域活動に参加する: join a community activity
Misuse note: Use に with 参加する. 催し is read もよおし, not from the on-reading of 催.

Japanese: 事故防止の対策を講じる
Kana: じこぼうしのたいさくをこうじる
Romaji: jiko boushi no taisaku o koujiru
Meaning: to take measures to prevent accidents
Usage note: The purpose modifies 対策 with の, and the measures taken take を with 講じる.
Example 1 (Japanese): 点検結果を受けて事故防止の対策を講じた。
Example 1 (English): We took accident-prevention measures in response to the inspection findings.
Example 2 (Japanese): 担当者と期限を決めて事故防止の対策を講じる。
Example 2 (English): We assign an owner and deadline when taking accident-prevention measures.
Contrast: 安全対策を取る: take safety measures / 事故を防止する: prevent accidents
Misuse note: Use を with 講じる. Name the hazard, measure, responsible party, and follow-up evidence.

Kana: いちがいにはいえない
Usage note: 一概に modifies the judgment; は commonly adds contrast before the negative 言えない.
Example 1 (Japanese): 利用者が増えたから成功したとは一概には言えない。
Example 1 (English): It cannot be said categorically that the project succeeded merely because user numbers rose.
Example 2 (Japanese): 条件が地域ごとに違うため一概には言えない。
Example 2 (English): It cannot be generalized because conditions differ by region.
Contrast: 必ずしもそうとは限らない: that is not necessarily so / 一律には扱えない: cannot be treated uniformly
Misuse note: Use 一概に with a negative predicate. State which variables prevent a general conclusion.

Japanese: 安堵の表情を浮かべる
Kana: あんどのひょうじょうをうかべる
Meaning: to show an expression of relief
Usage note: 安堵 modifies 表情 with の, and the expression shown takes を with 浮かべる.
Example 1 (Japanese): 家族の無事を知って安堵の表情を浮かべた。
Example 1 (English): On learning that the family was safe, she showed an expression of relief.
Example 2 (Japanese): 本人の言葉も聞かず安堵の表情を浮かべたと決めつけない。
Example 2 (English): We do not assume someone looked relieved without also hearing what they said.
Contrast: 安堵する: feel relieved / 胸をなで下ろす: breathe a sigh of relief
Misuse note: Use 安堵の表情, not 安堵な表情. In reporting, distinguish observation from inference.

Kana: ひみつをまもる
Usage note: The secret or confidential information protected takes を with 守る.
Example 1 (Japanese): 相談者の秘密を守ると約束した。
Example 1 (English): I promised to keep the person's disclosure confidential.
Example 2 (Japanese): 共有範囲を確認して秘密を守る。
Example 2 (English): I confirm who may receive the information and keep it confidential.
Contrast: 規則を守る: obey a rule / 約束を守る: keep a promise
Misuse note: Use を with 守る. In professional settings, explain any applicable limits instead of making an absolute promise.

Kana: せいめいをはっぴょうする
Usage note: The statement released takes を with 発表する. 公式声明 can specify formal status.
Example 1 (Japanese): 団体は調査結果を受けて声明を発表した。
Example 1 (English): The organization issued a statement in response to the investigation findings.
Example 2 (Japanese): 声明を発表する際に日付と発表主体を明記した。
Example 2 (English): When issuing the statement, we identified its date and issuer.
Contrast: 声明を出す: issue a statement / 見解を示す: state a view
Misuse note: Use を with 発表する. Quote or summarize an official statement with its issuer and date.

Kana: しつぼうをかくせない
Meaning: to be unable to hide one's disappointment
Usage note: The emotion one cannot conceal takes を with 隠せない.
Example 1 (Japanese): 期待していた結果ではなく失望を隠せなかった。
Example 1 (English): It was not the result I had hoped for, and I could not hide my disappointment.
Example 2 (Japanese): 本人は会見で失望を隠せないと語った。
Example 2 (English): At the press conference, the person said they could not hide their disappointment.
Contrast: 結果に失望する: be disappointed by the result / 落胆の色を見せる: show signs of dejection
Misuse note: Use を with 隠せない. Attribute emotional claims when reporting on another person.

Japanese: 思わぬ展開に呆気にとられる
Kana: おもわぬてんかいにあっけにとられる
Romaji: omowanu tenkai ni akke ni torareru
Meaning: to be dumbfounded by an unexpected turn
Usage note: The event causing surprise takes に. 呆気にとられる is a fixed expression and is usually written あっけにとられる in lighter prose.
Example 1 (Japanese): 議論が突然終わるという思わぬ展開に呆気にとられた。
Example 1 (English): I was dumbfounded by the unexpected turn in which the discussion suddenly ended.
Example 2 (Japanese): 知らせを聞いた直後は思わぬ展開に呆気にとられた。
Example 2 (English): Immediately after hearing the news, I was dumbfounded by the unexpected turn.
Contrast: 驚く: be surprised / 言葉を失う: be lost for words
Misuse note: Use に for the cause. Do not analyze とられる here as an ordinary passive of 取る.

Japanese: 波瀾万丈な人生を送る
Kana: はらんばんじょうなじんせいをおくる
Meaning: to lead an eventful life full of dramatic changes
Usage note: 波瀾万丈 takes な before 人生, and the life led takes を with 送る.
Example 1 (Japanese): 本人は自伝で波瀾万丈な人生を送ったと振り返る。
Example 1 (English): In the autobiography, the author looks back on having led an eventful life full of dramatic changes.
Example 2 (Japanese): 出来事を列挙するだけで波瀾万丈な人生を送ったと決めつけない。
Example 2 (English): We do not label a life dramatic merely by listing events.
Contrast: 波乱の多い人生を送る: lead a turbulent life / 穏やかな人生を送る: lead a peaceful life
Misuse note: In this predicate use, 波瀾万丈な人生 is standard. The variant spelling 波乱万丈 is also seen.

Japanese: 大規模な調査を実施する
Kana: だいきぼなちょうさをじっしする
Romaji: daikibo na chousa o jisshi suru
Usage note: 大規模 takes な before a noun; the survey conducted takes を with 実施する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 対象地域を広げて大規模な調査を実施した。
Example 1 (English): We expanded the target area and conducted a large-scale survey.
Example 2 (Japanese): 標本の選び方を公開して大規模な調査を実施する。
Example 2 (English): We disclose the sampling method when conducting a large-scale survey.
Contrast: 全国調査を行う: conduct a nationwide survey / 小規模な調査を行う: conduct a small-scale survey
Misuse note: Use 大規模な before a noun. Report sample, field dates, question wording, and method as well as size.

Kana: せいきょをいたむ
Usage note: The passing mourned takes を with 悼む. 逝去 is a respectful, formal noun.
Example 1 (Japanese): 教え子たちは恩師の逝去を悼んだ。
Example 1 (English): The former students mourned their teacher's passing.
Example 2 (Japanese): 関係者は静かに逝去を悼んだ。
Example 2 (English): Those concerned quietly mourned the passing.
Contrast: 死を悼む: mourn a death / 訃報に接する: learn of someone's death
Misuse note: Use を with 悼む. Avoid using the honorific 逝去 for one's own side when conventional in-group modesty is required.

Kana: きぐのこえがあがる
Usage note: 危惧 modifies 声 with の, and the voices arising take が with 上がる.
Example 1 (Japanese): 計画の安全性をめぐって危惧の声が上がった。
Example 1 (English): Concerns were raised about the plan's safety.
Example 2 (Japanese): 誰のどのような危惧の声が上がったのかを記事に記した。
Example 2 (English): The article stated whose concerns were raised and what they were.
Contrast: 将来を危惧する: fear for the future / 懸念が示される: concerns are expressed
Misuse note: Use 危惧の声, not 危惧な声. Replace vague attribution with named or accurately bounded sources when possible.

Kana: こうほをふるいにかける
Usage note: The items screened take を; 篩にかける is a metaphor meaning to filter or screen.
Example 1 (Japanese): 明示した条件に沿って候補を篩にかけた。
Example 1 (English): We screened the candidates according to the stated conditions.
Example 2 (Japanese): 基準と異議申立ての手順を公開して候補を篩にかける。
Example 2 (English): We publish the criteria and appeal process when screening candidates.
Contrast: 候補を絞る: narrow the candidates / 応募者を選考する: evaluate applicants
Misuse note: Write ふるいにかける in general-audience prose if the kanji is distracting. For people, 選考する is often more neutral.

Japanese: 世論の風向きが変わる
Kana: よろんのかざむきがかわる
Meaning: for the direction of public opinion to shift
Usage note: 世論 modifies the metaphorical 風向き with の; what changes takes が.
Example 1 (Japanese): 複数の調査で世論の風向きが変わったことが示された。
Example 1 (English): Several surveys indicated that the direction of public opinion had shifted.
Example 2 (Japanese): 一回の調査だけで世論の風向きが変わったとは判断しない。
Example 2 (English): We do not judge from a single survey that public opinion has shifted.
Contrast: 世論が変化する: public opinion changes / 支持が広がる: support grows
Misuse note: Use の and が as shown. Give dates, population, method, and uncertainty when the claim rests on polls.

Kana: ざいせいをたてなおす
Usage note: The finances being restored take を with 立て直す.
Example 1 (Japanese): 市は支出と収入を見直して財政を立て直した。
Example 1 (English): The city reviewed spending and revenue and restored its finances.
Example 2 (Japanese): 住民サービスへの影響も示して財政を立て直す案を比較する。
Example 2 (English): We compare plans to restore finances while also showing their effects on resident services.
Contrast: 財政を改善する: improve public finances / 財政が悪化する: public finances deteriorate
Misuse note: Use を with 立て直す. Do not equate a single balance figure with complete fiscal health.

Kana: じんけんをそんちょうする
Usage note: The rights respected take を with 尊重する.
Example 1 (Japanese): すべての利用者の人権を尊重する方針を定めた。
Example 1 (English): We adopted a policy to respect the human rights of every user.
Example 2 (Japanese): 当事者の意見を聞きながら人権を尊重する手順を見直す。
Example 2 (English): We review procedures for respecting human rights while hearing from those affected.
Contrast: 人権を守る: protect human rights / 人格を尊重する: respect a person's dignity
Misuse note: Use を with 尊重する. In legal contexts, identify the specific right and consult current authoritative sources.

Kana: むいむさくをひはんする
Meaning: to criticize a lack of effective action
Usage note: The alleged inaction criticized takes を. 無為無策 is strongly condemnatory.
Example 1 (Japanese): 野党は災害対応の無為無策を批判した。
Example 1 (English): The opposition criticized the lack of effective action in the disaster response.
Example 2 (Japanese): 記事では発言者を示して無為無策を批判する言葉を引用した。
Example 2 (English): The article attributed the words criticizing a lack of action to the speaker.
Contrast: 対応の遅れを批判する: criticize a delayed response / 具体策を求める: call for concrete measures
Misuse note: Use を with 批判する. Attribute the label and state the specific omitted or inadequate action.

Kana: よていひょうをかくにんする
Usage note: The schedule checked takes を with 確認する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 会議室を予約する前に予定表を確認した。
Example 1 (English): I checked the schedule before reserving the meeting room.
Example 2 (Japanese): 変更がないか朝に予定表を確認する。
Example 2 (English): I check the schedule in the morning for any changes.
Contrast: 予定を確認する: confirm plans / 予定表に記入する: enter something on a schedule
Misuse note: Use を for what you check and に for where you enter an item.

Kana: せいさくをうちだす
Usage note: The policy announced or advanced takes を with 打ち出す.
Example 1 (Japanese): 政府は住宅費の負担を減らす政策を打ち出した。
Example 1 (English): The government put forward a policy to reduce the burden of housing costs.
Example 2 (Japanese): 財源と開始時期も示して政策を打ち出す。
Example 2 (English): The government puts forward the policy while also stating its funding source and start date.
Contrast: 政策を発表する: announce a policy / 政策を実施する: implement a policy
Misuse note: Use を with 打ち出す. Distinguish a proposal or announcement from an enacted and implemented measure.

Kana: こうれいかがすすむ
Usage note: The demographic process takes が with 進む.
Example 1 (Japanese): この地域では全国平均より速く高齢化が進んでいる。
Example 1 (English): Population aging is advancing faster in this area than the national average.
Example 2 (Japanese): 年齢別人口の推移を見て高齢化が進む速度を比べる。
Example 2 (English): We compare the pace of population aging by examining population trends by age.
Contrast: 高齢者が増える: the number of older people increases / 少子化が進む: the birthrate decline advances
Misuse note: Use が with 進む. Cite the reference population, age threshold, dates, and source for quantitative claims.

Kana: しゃかいをふうしする
Usage note: The target of satire takes を with 風刺する.
Example 1 (Japanese): この小説は誇張と皮肉を使って社会を風刺している。
Example 1 (English): This novel uses exaggeration and irony to satirize society.
Example 2 (Japanese): 作品の時代背景を調べてから社会を風刺する表現を読む。
Example 2 (English): I examine the work's historical context before interpreting expressions that satirize society.
Contrast: 政治を風刺する: satirize politics / 社会を批判する: criticize society
Misuse note: Use を for the target. Separate textual evidence, creator statements, and your own interpretation.
